2073590502457590030.name: Derek Wen｜德里克文
2073590502457590030.text:
【AI绘画每日一词】品牌视觉套件
很多人理解 AI 生图，还停留在：
“帮我做一张海报。”
“帮我画一个 Logo。”
“帮我出一张包装图。”
但它真正更强的能力，其实是直接帮你搭一整套品牌视觉系统。
从品牌定调、视觉系统、产品包装，到门店传播场景，连续生成一整套统一风格的提案图。

如果你是做品牌、做餐饮、做门店、做项目汇报，尤其是奶茶店这类强调“颜值 + 传播 + 落地感”的项目，这个玩法真的非常实用。

我这里把它整理成一个更适合奶茶品牌的版本

🎯 核心提示词：

请根据以下品牌信息，创作一套高完成度、具有统一视觉系统的「4张品牌视觉提案图」。

注意：
这不是四宫格拼图，也不是把4张内容合并在同一个画面里的总图，而是4张需要依次分别生成的独立图片。
4张图必须属于同一个品牌视觉系统，但每一张承担不同职责，不能只是重复变体。

【品牌信息】
品牌名：天马奶茶
英文辅助名：TIANMA TEA
品牌类型：年轻化东方茶饮品牌 / 新中式轻奶茶品牌
一句话定位：把东方茶饮做得更轻盈、更清爽、更适合年轻人日常打卡和分享。
Slogan：这一杯，刚好是喜欢的样子。

核心关键词：
新中式、轻盈、清爽、年轻化、东方审美、茶感、奶香、果香、日常治愈、拍照分享、通透感、器物感

目标人群：
18–35岁年轻人，喜欢奶茶、拍照打卡、精致外卖、轻社交、视觉审美和品牌体验感的人群。

整体风格方向：
年轻、清爽、通透、克制、轻东方、有留白、有器物感、有产品层次感。
不是传统老派茶铺，也不是廉价网红风奶茶店，而是更年轻的新中式茶饮品牌。

主色调：
米白、茶叶绿、奶油白、雾青色、乌龙灰、琥珀茶棕

辅助色：
浅杏色、木质浅棕、冷灰、淡竹青

点缀色：
少量蜜桃粉、柠檬黄、西柚橙，仅用于个别产品提亮

辅助图形：
水波纹、茶叶轮廓、印章、小签条、东方线框、杯型轮廓、茶汤弧线、珍珠 / 椰果 / 柠檬片 / 茶叶 icon

器皿风格：
透明外带杯、磨砂杯、冷泡瓶、白瓷杯、玻璃杯、木托盘、纸袋、封签、杯套、杯垫

核心产品：
1. 招牌天马奶绿
2. 轻乌龙奶茶
3. 茉莉轻乳茶
4. 柠檬冰茶
5. 桃桃乌龙
6. 黑糖珍珠鲜奶

【统一要求】
1. 四张图必须属于同一个品牌系统，品牌名、配色、字体气质、辅助图形、包装逻辑、产品逻辑保持统一。
2. 所有图片统一采用竖版 4:5，适合社交媒体展示和品牌提案展示。
3. 每张图独立生成，不要四宫格，不要拼成一张总图。
4. 整体要有高完成度、信息量足够、设计感强、品牌提案感强。
5. 不要太古风，不要太老字号，不要太像糖水铺。要突出新中式、年轻化、轻茶感、清爽奶茶品牌。
6. 中文标题要清晰，英文字样仅作辅助，版式要有设计感。
7. 产品必须真实可口，茶汤层次清晰，杯型精致，包装统一。
8. 4张图依次生成：第1张→第2张→第3张→第4张。

【第1张图】
IMAGE 1｜BRAND HERO BOARD / 品牌主视觉封面

任务：
生成整套提案的封面图。第一眼就让人感受到：年轻、新中式、清爽、有茶感、有品牌感。

画面结构：
- 顶部：品牌名“天马奶茶”、英文辅助名“TIANMA TEA”、slogan“这一杯，刚好是喜欢的样子。”
- 中部：以一杯“招牌天马奶绿”为核心主视觉，透明杯或磨砂杯，清晰看到奶绿茶底、奶盖或轻乳层、杯壁水珠与通透质感
- 周围：适量摆放茶叶、奶香元素、柠檬片、乌龙茶叶、木托盘、小印章、东方光影等
- 底部：展示4个主打产品小卡片：招牌天马奶绿、轻乌龙奶茶、茉莉轻乳茶、桃桃乌龙；加入卖点icon：茶感清爽、真材实料、东方轻饮、适合打卡

要求：
画面要像高完成度品牌封面，不要像普通奶茶海报。要有品牌提案感、产品食欲感、年轻东方感。

【第2张图】
IMAGE 2｜VISUAL SYSTEM BOARD / 品牌视觉系统档案

任务：
生成品牌识别系统图，展示品牌视觉是如何构成的。比第1张更系统化，但依然保持清爽、年轻、新中式气质。

画面结构：
- 顶部：品牌名、英文辅助名、slogan，右侧可搭配一杯代表性奶茶图像
- 中部模块化展示以下内容：
  1）品牌标识系统：中文“天马奶茶”、英文“TIANMA TEA”、简化品牌印章或辅助图形
  2）色彩系统：米白、茶叶绿、奶油白、雾青色、乌龙灰、琥珀茶棕、浅杏色
  3）字体系统：中文标题字体、正文字体、英文辅助字体
  4）图标系统：茶叶、珍珠、椰果、奶盖、柠檬片、桃子、杯型等
  5）标签系统：东方轻饮、清爽奶茶、真材实料、低负担茶感、年轻化打卡、每日一杯
  6）辅助图形系统：水波纹、茶汤弧线、小签条、杯型轮廓、东方线条结构
- 底部：展示6个产品小卡片：招牌天马奶绿、轻乌龙奶茶、茉莉轻乳茶、柠檬冰茶、桃桃乌龙、黑糖珍珠鲜奶；每个有小图、icon和简短说明

要求：
不要做成普通VI手册，要更像“奶茶品牌视觉系统档案板”，信息丰富但有秩序，适合提案展示。

【第3张图】
IMAGE 3｜PRODUCT & PACKAGING BOARD / 产品与包装应用图

任务：
生成产品与包装应用图，展示这个品牌如何落地为可售卖的茶饮系统。

画面结构：
- 顶部：陈列4个重点产品：招牌天马奶绿、轻乌龙奶茶、桃桃乌龙、黑糖珍珠鲜奶；使用透明杯、磨砂杯、冷泡瓶等不同器皿呈现，茶汤层次清晰，真实可口
- 中部：展示包装和物料延展，包括外带杯、杯套、封签、纸袋、手提袋、菜单卡、点单贴纸、外卖贴签、双杯分享装等；统一延续品牌系统
- 底部：展示6个完整产品卡片：招牌天马奶绿、轻乌龙奶茶、茉莉轻乳茶、柠檬冰茶、桃桃乌龙、黑糖珍珠鲜奶；加入卖点：清爽茶感、真材实料、低负担、每日推荐、打卡友好

要求：
必须有“真能卖”的感觉。不能只是堆产品，要体现包装感、系统感、品牌感和商业落地感。

【第4张图】
IMAGE 4｜CAMPAIGN & SPACE BOARD / 传播与场景应用图

任务：
生成传播与场景应用图，展示《天马奶茶》进入真实场景后的品牌传播效果和空间体验。

画面结构：
- 左侧大主场景：展示“年轻化新中式奶茶店”门店场景，门头写“天马奶茶”，带英文辅助“TIANMA TEA”，店面干净、清爽、有轻东方元素，不要老派
- 右上：展示商场快闪或小型茶饮摊位，包含品牌海报、产品展示、小菜单、包装陈列
- 右中：展示两张宣传海报，一张主打招牌天马奶绿，一张主打桃桃乌龙或黑糖珍珠鲜奶；海报文案可用“这一杯，刚好是喜欢的样子。”“喝一口，刚好轻松下来。”
- 左下：模拟3–4张手机竖图式社媒内容，可包括新品推荐、门店打卡、今日推荐、真材实料展示
- 右下：展示品牌纸袋、纸巾、杯垫、封签、小卡片、外卖贴等品牌触点
- 底部：加入应用场景标签：新中式茶饮、年轻打卡、东方轻饮、日常治愈、真材实料；可加一句情绪化标语：“今天，也值得来一杯。”

要求：
比第3张更有场景感和故事感。不是廉价奶茶店，也不是高冷咖啡馆，而是年轻化、清爽、有传播力的新中式奶茶品牌。

【执行方式】
请严格按照以下流程执行：
1. 先内部理解并统一品牌视觉DNA。
2. 然后开始生成第1张图：品牌主视觉封面。
3. 在保持同一品牌系统的前提下，继续生成第2张图：品牌视觉系统档案。
4. 在保持同一品牌系统的前提下，继续生成第3张图：产品与包装应用图。
5. 在保持同一品牌系统的前提下，继续生成第4张图：传播与场景应用图。
6. 不要把4张图合并成一张，不要四宫格，不要让4张图内容重复。
7. 这是同一个品牌的连续4张提案图，不是4个不同项目。

【最终目标】
输出一套4张独立但高度统一的《天马奶茶》品牌视觉提案图：
- 第1张负责定调
- 第2张负责解释系统
- 第3张负责产品落地
- 第4张负责传播与场景落地

整套结果应具备：
统一的品牌视觉DNA、清晰的页面分工、高完成度的审美、商业提案感、展示感、作品集质量，以及可直接用于品牌概念展示的效果。

这个开源项目的海报风格太能打了！

我挑了其中 6 种风格作为参考，给同一家咖啡店制作了 6 张完全不同的海报。

瑞士极简、复古旅行、Riso 印刷、电影黑色、包豪斯、粗野主义。

同样的主题，换一种设计语言，出来的视觉效果完全不同。

项目叫 Fantastic Posters，是一套开源的 Skill。

它内置了 33 种经过设计的风格提示词，支持自动选择风格、上传参考图和 Logo，还能批量生成不同方案。

我觉得最有价值的地方，是把设计风格做成了可以反复调用的 AI 工作流，而不只是一次性的提示词。

我擦😅😅

MOSS-Image 这个文生图的模型有料啊

左侧是 codex 生成的，右侧是MOSS-Image生成

Qwen-Image-2.1 生图也不错就是中文一直没调好

核心特点：

1. 超强文字渲染：在长文本基准 LongLongTextBench（LLTB）上平均文字覆盖率达 96.3%（英文 97.1%、中文 92.4%），显著领先其他开源模型（如 Qwen Image 2512 的 64.9%）。

2. 支持清晰、准确的中英文文字生成。
原生布局控制：可用 JSON 直接指定物体、文字内容及其边界框（bounding box），实现精确排版。

3. 超长提示词：支持最高约 4096 tokens 的提示词。

2083043634635788298.name: 歸藏(guizang.ai)
2083043634635788298.text:
发现了 Codex 一个非常牛逼的更新，好像没见他们宣传！

Codex 现在有专门给图像 Agent 做的 UI 模式了：

生成图片后，点击图片会单独弹出一个侧边栏预览窗口。在这里面，你可以直接对图片进行评论、擦除和调整大小。这完全是专门给 GPT Image 2.0 做的。

左上角有一个切换按钮，切换以后，聊天流里就只显示图像，不显示那些文案了。

这样你就可以专注于调整图像，快速看到聊天里生成的所有大图。

你可以多选图片，一并添加到输入框里，然后让 GPT 给你进行批量修改。

Cursor 2.4 发布：Subagents 并行与专业化、上下文隔离、可定制，集成 Nano Banana Pro 带来原生图像生成能力，Cursor Blame 可溯源，交互式澄清。

核心特性：Subagents
· 并行化与专业化：过去 AI Agents 只能按顺序处理任务。现在，Parent Agent 可以拆解任务并生成多个独立运行的 Subagents。它们可以并行工作，分别负责代码研究、终端命令执行和多文件编辑。
· 上下文净化：由于每个 Subagent 拥有独立的上下文空间，主对话框不再会被冗长的搜索日志或中间调试信息淹没。这有效解决了大模型在长对话中因干扰信息过多而导致的“逻辑漂移”问题。
· 定制化潜力：开发者可以定义自定义 Subagents，为其分配特定的模型、Prompt 和工具权限，使其成为处理特定模块的“专家”。

多模态集成：原生图像生成
编辑器内集成了 Nano Banana Pro 模型，让 Agent 具备了视觉产出能力。
· 从 UI 到代码的闭环：开发者可以直接要求 Agent 生成 UI 样板图或架构示意图。生成的图片会自动保存到项目的 assets/ 目录。
· 视觉引导：支持上传参考图。这对于你这类关注 0 到 1 快速原型构建的开发者来说，是极其强大的生产力利器，极大地缩短了从设计稿到功能代码的距离。

企业级治理：Cursor Blame
针对团队协作中“谁写了这段代码”的难题，Cursor 推出了 AI 版的 git blame：
· 透明化溯源：每一行代码都能追溯到是人类手写、AI 补全（Tab）还是 Agent 自动生成。
· 逻辑回溯：最强大的地方在于，点击某行代码可以关联到当时生成该代码的 AI 对话摘要。这为代码审查提供了极其珍贵的意图背景和推理过程。

交互式澄清
· 异步协作：当遇到不确定的需求时，Agent 会主动发起提问。更高效的是，它在等待你回答的过程中并不会停工，而是会继续处理其他不相关的任务（如读取文件、准备测试环境），一旦你回答，它会立即将反馈并入工作流。

Here are the principles and methods I use when writing prompts:

My Prompting Principles

1. Design templates, not fixed prompts.

I want people to adapt the structure to their own scenarios—whether it’s their favorite brand, city weather, stock market themes, mini pop-up stores, or turning an article into an infographic.
The key idea is to give users a flexible framework rather than locking them into a single use case.

2. Leverage the model’s native capabilities (search, world knowledge, reasoning).

For example, the city-weather prompt lets Gemini fetch real weather information for a given city and date.
The 3D mini stock-market prompt works similarly.
Infographic prompts rely on the model’s comprehension and summarization of the input article.

My Strategy for Building Nano Banana Pro

1. Start by using AI to build a working prototype for one specific scenario.

2. Then generalize it into a prompt template that can dynamically adapt based on user input.

The core idea is to let the model assemble the structure automatically and adapt to different scenarios without imposing artificial constraints, just like writing code, where you avoid hard-coding and instead keep flexible interfaces for composition.

About Prompt Length

Modern models are strong enough that token length isn’t a big concern.

I don’t spend much time optimizing or shortening prompts at the beginning—functionality comes first.
If needed, refinement can come later.

I mainly use GPT-5.1, GPT-4.5, and Gemini 3 Pro as my supporting tools. I send the same task to all of them in parallel, let each model generate its own output, and then choose whichever result turns out best.

让拔叔🧑‍🍳教你做红烧肉吧🥣！！看拔叔享受的表情，看来很美味了😋

感谢 katon大佬 @hellokaton 提供思路，我设计一套可落地商业化的提示词分享给大家。

使用方式：
把提示词复制到Nano Banana Pro，修改餐品、角色来源、使用语言、参考图（可选）即可生图。

这套提示词支持：

✅自定人物/角色
✅自定义输入语言
✅画风随角色自动变化
✅3:4 比例出图，适合发布各类社交平台

应用场景（欢迎补充）：

🥳娱乐场景：发布朋友圈等个人社交媒体
🍠商业场景：发布小红书获取垂直流量，接广/卖号/IP 变现
💻打工人场景：制作线下物料，例如官方菜谱、门店桌牌、课程讲义、包装插画、周边小册子等

 Prompt：

Hyper-detailed 3:4 vertical cooking-instruction comic series, high-resolution digital illustration, clean vector/painted look, 2×2 panel grid per page, multi-page sequence allowed.
[Aesthetic Philosophy]: "Every recipe becomes a warm, character-driven kitchen story told in tiny cinematic moments."
[Subject Input]:
餐品🍚: 「红烧肉」
角色来源🧑: 「电影汉尼拔中的拔叔」
使用语言📖: 「英文」
[Canon Style Priority - Existing Characters]:
* IF Character Origin indicates an existing, copyrighted character from a known film / animation / anime / manga / game / TV series, THEN: • Preserve the canonical design of that character: facial features, hairstyle, body type, costume elements, color palette, and signature accessories must match the original work. • Preserve the original art style of the source (e.g., Ghibli-style painting, specific anime linework, classic manga screentone style, 3D CGI look, etc.), and apply that style consistently across all panels and pages. • Do NOT mix the character with a conflicting or random art style that contradicts the original work (no forced “chibi” or “hyper-realistic” changes unless the user explicitly asks for a parody/alternate style). • The cooking scenario and recipe are new, but the visual identity and style must feel like a natural extension of the original series.
* IF Character Origin is “original character” or unspecified, follow the generic {Character Profile & Style} description as the primary style driver.
[INTELLIGENT STEP PLANNING WORKFLOW]:
1. From {Dish Name}, infer a realistic, everyday home-style recipe with clear atomic steps: ingredient prep → cooking → seasoning → plating → tasting.
2. Decompose into numbered steps with logical continuity; each step must contain exactly one main action.
3. Layout logic:
* Each page is a 3:4 vertical canvas with a strict 2×2 grid → 4 panels per page.
* Page 1 = Steps 1–4; Page 2 = Steps 5–8; Page 3 = Steps 9–12; continue if needed.
* If the final page has fewer than 4 steps, fill remaining panels with: • Finished dish close-up hero shot. • Character proudly presenting the dish on a plate. • Character tasting/enjoying the dish with a satisfied reaction. • Simple decorative panel (ingredients, steam, flavor icons) that still reinforces the recipe.
4. User never provides steps: the model must infer, structure, and distribute them autonomously.
5. All step numbers are continuous and never reset across pages (e.g., Step 1–4 → Step 5–8 → Step 9–12).
OPTION A: IF Character Profile is cute / chibi / cartoon / anime AND (Character Origin is original OR the original work itself is stylized in a cute/anime/cartoon way) (Playful Home Kitchen Mode)
[Action]:
* Treat each panel as a mini slice-of-life scene in a cozy kitchen.
* Emphasize dynamic, readable silhouettes of the same chef character performing one key action per step (washing, chopping, stir-frying, seasoning, plating, eating).
* Camera framing alternates between medium shots (waist-up) and medium-wide shots (whole body + stove/counter) while always keeping the cooking process clearly visible.
* Use storytelling body language: bouncing posture while cooking, big eye sparkles when seasoning, small sweat drops when rushing, hearts or stars when tasting the final dish.
[Detail Emphasis]: Food & Ingredients:
* Fresh produce rendered with juicy highlights, crisp edges, visible textures (leaf veins, tomato seeds, noodle strands, rice grains).
* Clear depiction of ingredients specific to {Dish Name}: noodles, eggs, tomatoes, kimchi, sesame oil, chili oil, etc., placed in bowls or on cutting boards.
* Steam wisps, subtle oil sheen, bubbling sauces, golden sear marks, and realistic color changes as food cooks.
Kitchen Tools & Environment:
* Everyday home kitchen setup: gas or induction stove, frying pan/wok, cutting board, knives, bowls, bottles of oil and sauces.
* Small cute appliances (toaster, rice cooker) and hanging utensils that support the cozy mood.
* Counter edges, cupboard lines, tiles, and shelves drawn with clean perspective but simplified shapes.
Character Performance:
* Single consistent character across all panels and pages: same hairstyle, face shape, clothing, proportions, line quality, and color palette.
* IF Character Origin is an existing IP: • Match the canonical chibi/anime/cartoon proportions and facial design from the original work. • Maintain the same stylization of eyes, nose, mouth, hair rendering, and clothing folds as that series.
* Exaggerated facial expressions (surprise, concentration, happiness, pride) with anime-style emotion symbols (sweat drops, star eyes, tiny flames of motivation).
* Hands clearly interacting with objects: gripping knife, holding spatula, pouring sauce, lifting bowl, presenting plate.
Text & Lettering:
* Step labels clearly marked in the chosen {Text Language}, e.g., “步骤一 / Step 1 / ステップ1”.
* Short, friendly instructions in speech balloons or small captions at the bottom of each panel; tone casual and encouraging.
* Handwritten or handwritten-style font with rounded, approachable shapes; consistent font across all pages.
Panel & Line Quality:
* Thin, clean panel borders; small but even gutters between panels; soft rounded corners if desired.
* Line art with consistent weight; slightly thicker outlines on main character and food compared to background.
* Bright, warm color palette with soft shadows and subtle gradients, prioritizing appetizing food tones.
[Background]:
* Soft, uncluttered kitchen backgrounds with simplified cabinets, tiles, and windows; avoid visual noise.
* Use warm accent colors (creamy whites, soft yellows, pastel blues/greens) to frame the character and food.
* Backgrounds fade into lighter tones behind speech bubbles for legibility.
[Interactive Schematics]:
* Small icons to hint time and heat: tiny clock symbol with “5 min”, small flame icons with “low/medium/high heat”.
* Arrows showing ingredients moving from cutting board into pan, or pouring sauces into bowls.
* Minimal overlays: tiny labels for special ingredients (e.g., “辣椒油 / chili oil”, “芝麻 / sesame”) in the chosen {Text Language}.
* No clutter: diagrams always secondary to main comic action.
[Artistic Title Style]:
* On the first page, optional top strip or dedicated mini-title panel: • Dish name in large, stylized lettering in the chosen {Text Language}. • Secondary small subtitle like “Easy Home Recipe” or “简单家常做法” in a simple sans-serif or rounded font. • Decorative motifs (noodles, eggs, chili, rice grains) framing the title.
* IF Character Origin is an existing IP, the title aesthetic should subtly echo the original logo/typography style (without copying exact logo shapes).
OPTION B: IF Character Profile is semi-realistic / mature manga / painterly OR the original work has a more realistic / cinematic style (Cinematic Kitchen Mode)
[Action]:
* Treat each panel as a small cinematic frame; focus on clear, plausible cooking actions.
* Alternate between close-ups of hands/ingredients and mid-shots of the character at the stove or counter.
* Motion conveyed with subtle action lines and realistic body mechanics rather than extreme exaggeration.
* Emphasize the transformation of ingredients into the final {Dish Name} across the sequence.
[Detail Emphasis]: Food & Ingredients:
* Nuanced rendering: visible moisture, translucent oil, browned edges, subtle reflections on sauces.
* Carefully painted textures for meat, vegetables, noodles, and rice; soft subsurface scattering on pale ingredients like onions or eggs.
* Tiny imperfections (uneven chop sizes, little charred spots) to make food look real and delicious.
Kitchen Tools & Environment:
* More detailed environment: metal reflections on pans, light reflections on ceramic bowls, faint scratches on cutting boards.
* Gas flames with bluish cores and orange tips; induction stoves with glowing rings; realistic pot handles and lids.
* Background props (spice jars, chopping block, folded kitchen towel) used sparingly to hint at realism.
Character Performance:
* Same character design rigorously preserved across all panels and pages: consistent facial structure, body proportions, outfit, and shading style.
* IF Character Origin is an existing realistic/mature-style IP: • Follow the show’s or manga’s canonical facial construction, proportions, and costuming. • Apply the same line density, shading method (hatching, screentones, painterly), and color logic used in the original work.
* Expressiveness more subtle: soft smiles, focused eyes, gentle eyebrow movement instead of exaggerated cartoon symbols.
* Hands and posture anatomically correct: believable knife grip, wrist angles, and weight distribution.
Text & Lettering:
* Step labels as clean, modern banners or corner tags: “Step 1 / Step 2” or equivalent in the chosen {Text Language}.
* Short, direct instructions in a legible sans-serif or humanist font, not too decorative, aligned neatly within each panel.
* Occasional small side notes, e.g., “add a pinch of salt” or “stir quickly to avoid sticking”.
Panel & Line Quality:
* Strong, consistent grid with sharp rectangular panels, precise gutters, and clear safe margins.
* Refined line art or painterly edges that remain coherent across all pages; no style drift.
* More controlled palette: rich but realistic food colors, slightly desaturated kitchen tones, focused highlights on key areas.
[Background]:
* Realistic yet unobtrusive kitchen setting: countertops, cabinets, and appliances correctly placed in perspective.
* Background detail density carefully balanced: sharper near the cooking area, softer and more blurred in the distance.
* Use of depth-of-field effects (soft blur) to emphasize focal points like hands or the pan.
[Interactive Schematics]:
* Minimal but precise overlays: • Small timer icons with minutes. • Heat level indicators (“low heat”, “medium-high heat”). • Measurement hints (“1 tsp”, “½ cup”).
* Occasional graceful arrows following the motion of pouring or stirring.
* All overlays integrated into the aesthetic, matching the overall font and line style.
[Artistic Title Style]:
* First page may include a refined title block: • Dish name in a bold serif or elegant display font. • Subtitle line such as “Home Kitchen Series” or localized equivalent. • Simple dividers or lines, no heavy graphic clutter.
* IF Character Origin is an existing IP, allow subtle echo of the original title-card mood (color palette, framing) without copying logos.
[Universal Composition]:
* Every page is a 3:4 vertical canvas with a strict 2×2 grid (four equal panels).
* Consistent panel ratio, gutter width, and outer margins across all pages in the sequence.
* Character and food remain well within safe zones (no critical content touching panel edges).
* Visual hierarchy: • Food and main action = primary focus. • Character’s face/body = secondary. • Background and overlays = tertiary.
* Sequence readability: left-to-right, top-to-bottom (or adjusted to locale if necessary), making the entire recipe easy to follow at a glance.
[Universal Lighting]:
* Warm, appetizing lighting as a baseline: key light from the front/side illuminating food and character.
* Soft shadows under bowls, pans, and utensils; mild bounce light from surrounding surfaces.
* Steam and glow effects around hot dishes; gentle specular highlights on glossy sauces and oils.
* Avoid overly dramatic or dark lighting that could obscure ingredients or text.
[Graphic Elements - The "Call-out" System]:
* Step numbers always clear, prominent, and sequential across pages (e.g., “步骤一…步骤八” or “Step 1…Step 8”).
* Three-tier text hierarchy: • Main Label: step number + 2–8 word summary of the action. • Sub-Label: short supporting instruction or tip if necessary. • Micro-Spec: optional tiny detail such as time, heat level, or quantity.
* Speech balloons (for character dialogue) clearly separated from instructional captions; balloons never cover critical food details.
* Fonts stay consistent in style, weight, and size hierarchy across the entire series.
[Artisan Signature Plaque]:
* Reserve a small, consistent area (e.g., bottom-left or bottom-right corner of each page) for a subtle signature system.
* Style: tiny emblem (e.g., miniature cutting board, spoon, or chef hat) with micro text like “Kitchen Story Series” or equivalent in {Text Language}.
* Flat or lightly embossed look; low contrast so it never competes with the main content; no logos, QR codes, or external branding.
[Global Constraints]:
* The same {Character Profile & Style} and, where applicable, the same canonical IP design must persist identically across all panels and pages: do not change age, face, hairstyle, outfit, or rendering style.
* The same overall art style (line work, coloring method, shading, texture level) must persist across the entire recipe sequence.
* Strictly no watermarks, logos, QR codes, UI buttons, or camera interface overlays.
* All outputs are high-resolution, print-ready 3:4 vertical images, each page a self-contained four-panel cooking comic.
Suggested model parameters: --ar 3:4 --q 2 --stylize 300

2044483458139853290.name: AmirMušić
2044483458139853290.text:
Prompt:   
(access Nano Banana 2 here: https://t.co/fVqOq1C1pU)

[BRAND NAME] | [COLOR]

Act as a 3D Motion Graphics Director and CGI Type Artist specializing in Japanese streetwear, Y2K motorsport aesthetics, and retro-tech hardware design. References: Kawasaki Racing livery, Yasuhiro Nightow title cards, Wipeout game UI, Peak Design × Japanese hardware collab.

PHASE 0: BRAND LOGO INTELLIGENCE

Retrieve the canonical logotype of [BRAND NAME] from training data. Identify its core typographic DNA — stroke weight, angle of italic lean, terminal style, any custom glyph cuts. If [BRAND NAME] uses a geometric or sans-serif wordmark — apply a 15 to 20° italic transformation while preserving all letterform proportions. If [BRAND NAME] already uses italic or script — preserve its native angle exactly. The goal is to translate the brand's typographic identity into a Japanese motorsport script register — aerodynamic, forward-leaning, built for speed. The letters must remain recognizable as [BRAND NAME]'s typeface, not replaced with a generic racing font.

PHASE 1: PRIMARY TYPOGRAPHY SCULPTURE

The wordmark of [BRAND NAME] is a fully 3D object — thick, physical, occupying real depth. Form language: each letter has a flat front face, beveled top and bottom edges with 30 to 45° chamfer cuts — the kind of angular geometry found on Japanese racing fairings and Kawasaki tank badges. Letters are slightly condensed and heavily italic — forward momentum is built into the geometry. The overall silhouette reads as one unified aerodynamic form — letters connect at their bases through a common ground plane, like a single cast aluminum piece. Material: high-gloss automotive lacquer in [COLOR] — the same paint system as a Japanese sports motorcycle tank. Surface properties: IOR 1.6, roughness 0.05, clear-coat depth visible. [COLOR] is pure and saturated in midtones, pushing toward near-white in specular peaks, pulling toward deep shadow in recessed zones and chamfer undersides. Reflections on the front face: subtle dark environment reflections — minimal and moody, just enough to show material depth. Top chamfer faces catch the primary light as bright highlight strips — the signature detail that defines 3D volume.

PHASE 2: NEON WIRE OUTLINE SYSTEM

A continuous neon tube traces the exact outer silhouette contour of the entire wordmark — every letter edge, every chamfer angle, every connecting point between letters. This is not a glow effect or a stroke — it is a physical glass neon tube, 4 to 6mm diameter, bent precisely to follow the letterform outline at a 3 to 5mm offset distance from the letter surface. Neon tube properties: glass tube body is semi-transparent — internal plasma glow visible through glass. Light emission: bright cold white light, color temperature 7000 to 8000K, pure white with very slight blue-cool bias. Emitted light creates a tight halo of illumination — 8 to 15mm radius soft glow on surrounding black void. The neon light bounces onto nearest letter surfaces — edges adjacent to the tube receive subtle cool white rim light. Tube construction: clean geometric bends at sharp corners, thin mounting wire clips at 3 to 4 points along its length — technically precise, like real neon sign hardware.

PHASE 3: INTEGRATED TECHNICAL SCREEN

A hardware screen panel is physically integrated with the wordmark — not a separate floating element, not placed at a distance. Integration logic — autonomously determine the most natural attachment point based on [BRAND NAME]'s logo geometry, choosing ONE of these integration modes: OVERLAP MODE — the screen panel is partially overlaid onto the rightmost or leftmost letter of the wordmark, as if mounted directly on the letter face. The letter surface shows through the screen's transparent zones. The screen edge cuts across the letter geometry deliberately — like a sticker or plate bolted onto the sculpture. EXTENSION MODE — the screen panel extends directly from the end of the final letter as a seamless continuation of the wordmark's ground plane — same italic angle, same 3D depth, as if the wordmark was designed with this panel as part of its original form. The transition from letter to screen feels like one continuous designed object. INSET MODE — the screen panel sits in a recess cut into one of the larger letters — as if a rectangular section of the letter body was removed and replaced with a hardware display. The letter geometry frames the screen on three sides.

Screen physical construction: machined aluminum or brushed steel housing, same thickness as the letter sculpture — 8 to 12mm deep. The face is a slightly frosted acrylic panel backlit from within. The screen has the same italic angle as the wordmark — it is not upright, it leans with the composition. Screen contents rendered in precise small-scale detail: [BRAND NAME] in small clean technical sans-serif as primary label. An alphanumeric model code autonomously generated to feel authentic to [BRAND NAME]'s cultural language. 2 to 3 Japanese characters as secondary label. A horizontal LED progress bar — 4 to 6 rectangular segments, 1 to 2 lit in amber, others dark. A small ventilation grille or mesh pattern along one edge of the housing. The screen connects to the neon outline system via 1 to 2 thin cables — physical wires, 1 to 2mm diameter, with slight organic sag from gravity, running to the nearest neon tube mounting clip.

PHASE 4: LIGHTING & ATMOSPHERE

Background: pure absolute black (#000000 to #030303) — complete void, no ambient, no gradient, no surface. The composition is self-illuminated — only light sources are the neon tube emission, the screen's internal backlight, and a single narrow overhead spot. Overhead spot: focused directly above the wordmark center — illuminates top chamfer faces as bright highlight strips, falls off completely within 5 to 10cm of letterform edges, never reaches the background. Neon contribution: cool white rim light on adjacent letter edges, 8 to 15mm glow halo in surrounding void, reflected light on cables and screen housing. Screen contribution: the frosted acrylic face emits a soft diffused glow — slightly cooler than the neon, illuminating the immediate area of whichever letter the screen is integrated with. The amber LED segments create a warm micro-glow within the screen housing. No other light sources. No rim lights. No fill. Darkness is absolute outside self-illuminated zones.

PHASE 5: COMPOSITION

Aspect ratio: 1:1 square. The wordmark with integrated screen occupies the horizontal center — wider than tall, spreading laterally. The screen integration should feel like it was always part of the logo design — not an accessory bolted on, but a native component. Vertical position: slightly above center. The neon outline breaches the implied bounding box slightly at 1 to 2 points — confirming physical separation between neon tube and letter surface. Camera: slightly elevated 5 to 10° above center — reveals top chamfer faces and confirms 3D depth. Mild perspective. Depth of field: none — sharp across entire composition from screen detail to neon tube.

PHASE 6: TECH SPECS

Render: Octane Render or Redshift. Ray tracing: on — for accurate neon tube emission, screen backlight glow, glass refraction, cable shadows. Volumetric light: subtle around neon tube and screen face only — physically present glow without fogging the black void. Neon tube: dielectric glass material with physical light emission, not a glow map. Screen face: translucent acrylic with internal emissive backlight. Letter sculpture: automotive lacquer with full clear-coat depth. Anti-aliasing: maximum. Sampling: minimum 1024 samples. Film grain: none. Output feel: CGI title card or album cover — precision and atmosphere in equal measure. Darkness absolute. Neon and screen physically real.

2000362419475132676.name: 小羊驼杂记
2000362419475132676.text:
地貌博物馆

示例：中国的地貌
1. 喀斯特地貌
2.风成地貌
3.流水地貌
4.褶皱山地貌

输入：国家+地貌名称
生成：浮空岛（该国地图形状）上的地貌景观，结合相关的地理构造以及人文景观元素。

👇👇👇
---
提示词规则（两段式，基于此生成nano banana pro提示词，将其输入后生成图片，英文版见评论区）

### 角色定义
你是一名 **构造地理造景师**。你的目标是将一个国家可视化为一个体积感十足、漂浮的地壳，其形状严格遵循该国地图的轮廓。你必须创造一种戏剧性的视觉效果：夸张的地表地形、深层的地质剖面，以及宏伟的地标建筑，并由适应生物群落的动态、有组织的人群所填充。

---

### 核心能力
**视觉策略（戏剧性的切片）：**

- **体积与结构基础：** 岛屿是一块厚实的板块。侧面悬崖揭示了土地的内部故事（地层、岩浆脉络、根系），在视觉上支撑着地表。
- **夸张的地表地形：** 不要只是给地图加纹理，而是要雕刻它。如果是“山脉”，地图表面必须呈现巨大的脊柱状山脊；如果是“峡谷”，地图必须深裂。地貌必须在远处即可一眼辨认。
- **宏伟地标聚焦：** 国家最著名的建筑必须被放大并突出。它不应融入背景，而应作为地形的“皇冠明珠”骄傲地矗立（例如：宫殿位于最高峰之巅）。
- **动态有序的人群：**
- 避免：静止、孤立的人物随意站立。
- 使用：有组织的队列（商队、军队、宗教游行、迁徙）。他们必须有方向和目的，在地图上形成流动的线条。
- 约束：如果历史数据模糊，则使用通用但有组织的、符合生物群落的群体（如“游牧牧民”），而不是虚构具体的军事单位。
- **情境逻辑：** 服饰与建筑材料必须严格遵循 {TARGET_LANDFORM} 的气候条件。

---

### 工作流程（内部“思维链”）
基于 {TARGET_COUNTRY} 和 {TARGET_LANDFORM}：
1. **雕刻地图：** 创建三维地壳，使地表地形具有强烈的视觉冲击。
2. **放置地标：** 确定最具代表性的建筑，并战略性地安置（最高点/中心）。
3. **引导人群：** “他们要去哪里？”绘制人群的流动线（例如：丝绸之路商队蜿蜒穿越沙丘）。
4. **纹理侧面：** 展示支撑该特定地貌的地质结构。

---

### 输出格式（最终提示词）
你将输出一个针对结构叙事幻想优化的单一提示块：

**提示结构：**

**[1. 体积地图岛屿]**
一块雄伟厚重的漂浮地壳，形状严格遵循 {TARGET_COUNTRY} 的地图轮廓，悬浮在戏剧性的天空中。岛屿被可视化为地球的深层地质切片，而非平面。

**[2. 夸张的地貌（表面与边缘）]**
{TARGET_LANDFORM} 以戏剧性的视觉冲击呈现：
- **表面（视觉识别）：** 顶部表面具有高度夸张、突出的地形特征，鲜明体现 {TARGET_LANDFORM}（如锋利的脊柱状山脊、深裂的峡谷或巨大的陨石坑），在地图正面形成视觉主导。
- **垂直边缘（结构地质）：** 漂浮基座的陡峭悬崖揭示支撑地形的内部地质：[扭曲的岩层 / 沉积层 / 暴露的岩浆脉络 / 巨大的根系]，增加科学深度。

**[3. 宏伟建筑（视觉焦点）]**
{TARGET_COUNTRY} 最具代表性的建筑杰作作为岛屿的视觉锚点与皇冠明珠。它被放大以突出，戏剧性地安置在 [例如：最高峰之巅 / 瀑布边缘]，与狂野地形形成对比，同时使用当地材料。

**[4. 动态有序的人群（叙事流动）]**
景观中不是静止人物，而是有目的地移动的动态、有组织的小型人群。他们的服饰严格适应 {TARGET_LANDFORM} 的气候：
- **队列形式：** [根据情境选择：商队蜿蜒穿越地形 / 军团整齐行进 / 宗教游行攀登小径 / 游牧部落携牲畜迁徙]。
- **视觉流动：** 人群在地图上形成流动线条，增添生命力与尺度感。
- **无时代错位：** 不出现现代游客、手机或散乱的个体。

**[5. 生物群落文字设计]**
在地质剖面附近漂浮着三维文字“{TARGET_COUNTRY}: {TARGET_LANDFORM}”。字母由 {TARGET_LANDFORM} 的材质（如花岗岩、冰、砂岩）雕刻而成，仿佛是岛屿的自然延伸。

**[6. 氛围与技术细节]**
史诗般的结构场景。电影级灯光，强烈阴影突出地形。8k 分辨率，移轴摄影风格，Octane 渲染，Unreal Engine 5。
--禁止方形边框、平面地图、纸质地图、智能手机、相机、游客、静止姿态、杂乱人群
--ar 16:9 --stylize 900 --v 6.0

---

### 用户输入变量
请生成以下目标的提示词：
**{TARGET_COUNTRY} = 中国**
**{TARGET_LANDFORM} = 褶皱山脉地貌**

这也太强了！高级商业化！用 Nano Banana Pro 做出你的品牌美食宣传海报

这次可不得了，群友硬是改出一个超强的模版，你们要做的仅仅是把这套提示词加一个主体，然后给 Gemini 

如果出来满意的模版，继续出即可，当然你也可以多随机刷一些

提示词：
画面比例：9:16 竖版
画面风格（可根据主体调整）：高端商业摄影，暗调奢感，电影级质感，超写实，高细节
背景（可根据主体调整）：纯黑背景（#000000），无任何台座、无平台、无地面，主体与元素全部悬浮于空间中
【主体】
核心展示主体为：【用户提供的主体】
务必通过你的数据库只是和互联网搜索，将主体拆解为多个“可识别、可理解、具有层次关系的组成部分”，请根据主体特性自行判断并设计拆解逻辑与层级顺序。
【整体构图】
整体采用“垂直分层悬浮结构”，从上至下形成清晰的视觉阅读路径。
每一层之间存在明显空间间隔，层与层之间通过空气、蒸汽、光影产生联系，而非直接接触。
画面中央为视觉主轴，构图稳定但富有张力。
【标题系统（顶部）】
画面最上方正中位置，悬浮一个高端主标题：
文案内容由 AI 根据主体自动生成（可包含中文主标题 + 英文副标题）
字体风格（可根据主体调整）：手写毛笔书法风 / 自然书写感
材质（可根据主体调整）：立体金属质感，仿锻造金色金属
表现特征（可根据主体调整）：厚重、3D、具有真实金属反射、高光与暗部层次
【分层结构（中部主体区域）】
根据主体，自主生成 4–6 个逻辑清晰的悬浮层级，例如：
原料层 / 构成层 / 关键元素层 / 核心结构层 / 氛围或情绪层
每一层都具有明确材质、颜色、纹理与体积感
各层之间留有空气与空间，不拥挤、不堆叠
所有中间层：
均处于轻微蒸汽、热气或空气扰动之中
有细小颗粒、雾气、水汽或尘埃漂浮
受统一灯光系统控制，保持整体一致性
【过渡区（重要）】
在主体分层与最终呈现之间，刻意保留一个“明显更大的空间断层”：
此区域以空气、蒸汽、烟雾、能量流、光雾为主
不放置实体物体
作用是制造节奏、呼吸感与视觉落差
强化“从结构到成品 / 从过程到结果”的转折
【最终成品层（底部）】
画面最下方呈现完整、最终形态的主体：
状态为“完成态 / 高峰态 / 最具吸引力的呈现”
质感饱满、细节丰富、具有强烈诱惑力或感染力
与背景自然融合，但清晰突出
从该区域向上持续产生蒸汽、烟雾或能量感
【信息标注系统】
在画面中适度加入说明性标注：
中英文双语
文字克制、优雅
使用细线或箭头指向对应层级
标注内容由 AI 根据主体自动生成
不喧宾夺主，只起“高级解读”作用
【署名 / 品牌元素】
画面右下角：
悬浮一个品牌署名或签名式 Logo
风格与主标题一致（毛笔字感、金属金色、立体等）
可搭配轻微星光、微闪效果，强调高级感
在底部有一句针对主体的一句话商业爆款SLOGAN
【光影系统】
45° 方向专业影棚灯光
暖色轮廓光（rim light）勾勒结构边缘
局部高光突出材质真实感
蒸汽与烟雾被灯光切割，形成体积光
【整体气质】
暗调、克制、昂贵  或底部一侧（可根据主体调整）
具有“灵魂感 / 温度 / 手工感 / 高级商业审美”
适用于品牌海报、主视觉、封面级商业展示

可拓展性很大，这套提示词，本质在于拆分物件的素材、步骤等，然后加入了一些 SLOGAN 文案设计，如果你真的有自己的品牌，或者你想试试某些品牌，通过上传相关素材，继续调整，就能做出合格的宣传海报来了

2047489301064360130.name: AllenLei
2047489301064360130.text:
GPT-Image-2 比谷歌Nano Banana，到底强在哪？

一、两大顶尖AI生图模型核心本质区别

谷歌Nano Banana是极致专业设计师，纯按需作画，响应快、画质高，只精准执行指令；GPT-Image-2则是带队实操的设计总监+完整设计团队，不只是单纯作画，全程分流程精细化创作，具备自主思考统筹能力，综合实力远超前者。

底层核心逻辑天差地别：谷歌是给画画工具加推理能力，本质还是生图工具，上限有限；OpenAI是给超强推理大脑加装画画技能，核心是会思考再创作，发展天花板极高。行业Arena榜单数据佐证，GPT-Image-2领先第二名Nano Banana 2多达241分，创历史最大差距，属于量级式碾压。

二、GPT-Image-2三大颠覆性核心突破（核心竞争力）

1. 补齐核心基本功，文字渲染彻底封神
攻克AI生图多年顽疾文字乱码问题，英文菜单排版规范、拼写精准可直接商用；中文渲染实现质的飞跃，排版、笔画、偏旁零错误，日韩多语言同步完美适配。彻底告别以往AI出图后，人工手动二次加字修改的割裂工作模式，核心得益于研发核心团队大量中文背景从业者，懂中文使用习惯与排版逻辑。

2. 从听指令干活，升级为主动思考创作
不再需要精细繁琐提示词，无需用户预设所有细节。可自主读懂长文稿、70页专业PDF，自主提炼核心重点、梳理逻辑层级，独立完成信息图、书籍封面、成套PPT设计。如同设计总监先吃透需求核心，再自主规划创作方案，无需用户费心调教，全程自主统筹落地。

3. 实现系统性画面一致性，连贯创作无短板
解决AI生图最大痛点多图风格、人物形象不统一问题，单次最多生成8张连贯图片，人物外貌、服装造型、光影色调、画风风格全程精准统一。可轻松搞定穿搭系列图、连载连贯漫画等需求，无需后期人工手动对齐修改，一次生成即可直接使用。

三、普通人&职场人核心实用机遇

1. 提示词工程彻底失效，无需刻意学调教技巧，不用费心伺候AI，只需说清核心需求、交付素材，AI自主读懂、思考、创作，门槛大幅降低；

2. 内容创作效率翻倍，几分钟就能搞定各类商用视觉配图、海报物料，替代耗时的找图、修图、排版全流程；

3. 创业低成本起步，无需花钱聘请专职设计师，创业初期所有运营、产品视觉物料AI均可直接搞定，砍掉创业核心成本门槛；

4. 客户提案效率提速，一键生成多风格备选设计方案，从猜需求变选方案，决策效率直接翻倍。

四、模型现存短板（避坑提醒）

并非全能，精密三维物理逻辑内容（折纸步骤、魔方还原）、带精准箭头/部件标注的专业图表标签仍会出错，需人工审核核对即可规避问题。

五、AI生图发展三大阶段迭代

1. 初期：能用但画质差，纯娱乐玩具；

2. 中期：好看但需精细调教，催生提示词工程行业；

3. 现在：GPT-Image-2开启新阶段，只需说清需求，AI全程自主思考、统筹、创作落地。

Google 把「会修图」直接塞进 Docs 和 Slides。

9  1 起Google Workspace 正式上线 Pics：原生嵌进办公流的 AI 生图 + 对象级精修，聊框随出一张图就完事。Group Product Manager Meg Whittenberger 在 Workspace 官博写明，浏览器打开 https://t.co/cvAMqOpluU 就能用。TechCrunch 等也把它写成 Canva / Adobe Express 的对位产品。

底座是 Nano Banana。提示词生成，从电脑、Drive、Photos 导入；然后点选画面里单个物体改，改图内文字至直接翻译，成社媒打印尺寸，还能升到 2K、4K。在 Docs 或 Slides 里选中一张图，一点就能进 Pics 全套工具，不用切应用。协作跟 Docs 一样：享链接、Drive 存、多人一起改。接下来几周还能 Drive 里对几乎任意图片一打开编辑。

开放给 Business Standard / Plus、Enterprise Standard / Plus，以 Google AI Pro、Ultra，和教育版 AI Pro。对团队来说，设计从「去另一个网当设计师」变成「在正在写的文档里 prompt + 改物体」。

你们会更想在 Docs/Slides 里直接出图，还是继续把素材丢到单独的设计工具里做？

Nano Banana Pro 提示词

太可爱了，制作任何地方的天气移轴 Q 版模型！

从宝玉这个玩法来的灵感，优化了一下整个模型的视觉效果，现在更加软润可爱。

天气会以更加更加拟物化的方式呈现，你可以输入经纬度也可以写地点，文字排版也更加的精细。

海报设计、自媒体封面设计：查找经纬度位于 52.891970728167614, 122.4549778092535 的地点并且获取地点的天气和时间。

画面的主体是当地代表性的建筑或者景观轴侧微缩模型，上方是当前天气的微缩模型，比如云、太阳等。梦工厂风格，3D建模，细腻、柔和的光线投影，画面周围大面积留白，画面底部居中无衬线体小字写上位置信息和天气图标和时间以及中文位置介绍文案。高品质画面输出。

这个 Skill 一出，Logo设计师可以下岗了！

小米当时花了几百万请日本设计师改Logo，最后大家评价改了个寂寞。设计的玄学就是这么强。

最近在重构灯塔时需要新Logo，作为 AI 的重度用户就拉着AI一起来设计新Logo，前后30分钟从哲学思想到视觉设计一个Skill搞的明明白白的，最关键设计我很喜欢！

这个 Skill 就是：canvas-design

和一般设计不同的是，用canvas设计可以从哲学思想到视觉效果进行深度沟通以后直接出图。他不是简单的你让画啥就画啥，而是先从灵魂深层理解你的诉求最后再完成设计。

比较爽的是，一键生成PNG、SVG以及各种各样的布局和尺寸。安装使用方法也很简单：

npx skills add https://github。com/anthropics/skills --skill canvas-design --agent claude-code -y

2113553061771682209.name: Varun Chopra
2113553061771682209.text:
Ideogram just shipped Vector 1.0, its first model that outputs real SVGs instead of pixels. Prompt to an editable vector, or trace any image into one.

What builders should know:

1. Two endpoints, both async. POST /v2/svg/generate/ideogram-vector-1 turns a prompt into an SVG. /v2/svg/vectorize/ideogram-vector-1 converts a JPEG, PNG or WEBP (up to 50 MB). You get a generation_id back, so poll for the file or pass a webhook_url.

2. You pay per file, not per token. Text to vector is $0.13 low, $0.16 medium, $0.20 high, and $0.32 for high with reference images. Image to vector is $0.10 (fal's listed rates). Twelve medium logo drafts cost $1.92.

3. Quote before you spend. Add ?dry_run=true and the API validates and prices the request without generating or billing anything. Run it before you batch an icon set.

4. The vectorizer gotcha: its group option (shapes into layers) is marked "not yet available." A traced PNG logo comes back as paths, not a tidy layered file. Use mode=simple for fewer, cleaner shapes.

Worth trying: have your coding agent generate icons as SVG, so it can tweak the file's code instead of rerolling the image.

A PNG is a screenshot. An SVG is source code.

This prompt transforms virtually any text content—from blog posts and research papers to product introductions—into stunning information cards. 

Feel free to copy and use it 🔽🔽🔽

------ PROMPT START ------

Role: Modern Editorial Information Card Designer
You are the Modern Editorial Information Card Designer. Your task is to reconstruct user input text into a high-density, high-contrast HTML5 information card with magazine-level typography.

Core Design Philosophy
· Style: Compact Editorial. Think of it as a refined newspaper front page, a deep-dive sidebar, or a high-end museum label.
· Visual Identity: Reject cheap Tech Blue or generic Flat Design. Pursue paper texture, the strength of serif fonts, and data visualization.
· Layout: Strict grid system. No wasted whitespace.

Technical Specifications (Strictly Enforce)
· Output Format: Output only one complete HTML file. Do not include any explanations outside the code block.
· Libraries:
Tailwind CSS (via CDN).
FontAwesome (via CDN) for icons.
Google Fonts: Import Noto Serif SC (700, 900), Noto Sans SC (400, 500, 700), and Oswald (500, 700).

Visual Design Guidelines
1. Color Strategy (Retro/Industrial):
Background: # f2f0eb (Beige/Greige) or # e5e0d8 (Aged Paper).
Text: # 1a1a1a (Ink Black) or # 2c241b (Dark Brown).
Accent Color: Choose one high-saturation retro color, such as Hermès Orange (# c17c4a), Rust Red (# b83b18), or Prussian Blue (# 0f4c81).
Decoration: Use dark lines to divide sections.

2. Texture (Crucial Detail):
You MUST overlay a subtle SVG Noise texture (opacity 0.05-0.08) over the entire card to create a grainy paper feel.

3. Typography Rules:
Main Headline: Use Noto Serif SC, weight 900, line-height 0.9, massive font size (3.5rem+).
Numbers/Labels: Use Oswald, all caps, tall and narrow.
Body Text: Use Noto Sans SC, small but legible size, tight line height.

4. Shadows: Use deep diffused shadows or Brutalist hard-edge offset shadows.

Content Structure Template (Top-Down)
1. Header:
Left/Center: High-impact, massive serif headline.
Right/Corner: Small tags, date, or source using Oswald.
Bottom: Must have a thick divider line.

2. Intro (Lead/Pain Points):
A highlighted background block or a blockquote with a thick left border. Briefly state the core context or pain points.

3. Grid Body (Core Content):
Use grid-cols-2 or grid-cols-3.
Each card contains: Icon + Bold Subtitle + Concise Explanation.
Cards must be distinguished by borders or background colors.

4. Footer (Data Anchor):
Dark Background (White text).
Display core conclusions, key data (huge numbers), or a punchy quote.
This is the visual anchor; it must be striking.

Interactivity & Animation
Add simple entrance animations: Elements should fade in and float up (translate-y) sequentially using animation-delay.

Workflow
1. Analyze the user's input to extract: Title, Core Pain Points, Key Arguments (3-4 points), and Key Data/Conclusions.
2. Rewrite the copy: Make it concise and punchy, like News Headlines.
3. Code: Generate the HTML.

Now, please receive my content and start designing.

------ PROMPT END ------

2027768326852681798.name: Harshil Tomar
2027768326852681798.text:
90% of apps look vibe coded: 

same purple gradients, same default fonts, same AI slop.

Here’s a workflow to make your app look like it came from a real agency, not a model:

1/ Ship a boring prototype first

> Use Google AI Studio or Cursor to spit out a 1‑shot functional app (e.g. voice journaling).  
> Don’t touch the UI. Just list what actually exists now: screens, flows, edge cases.

Function first, vibe later.

2/ Decide how it should feel

> Ask Claude: who is this for, what state are they in, what feeling do we want?  
> Turn that into 1–2 paragraphs of brand guidelines: name, vibe words, “analog vs sci‑fi,” what to avoid.

You’re not designing a screen, you’re designing a mood.

3/ Build a reference bank

> Collect images on Pinterest / https://t.co/Mpq6TUUB02 / your own Notion: objects, textures, lighting, typography.  
> Think “cassette decks and paper notes” or “glass and neon,” not “UI shots.”

This becomes your visual prompt library.

4/ Generate on-theme assets

> Use Flux / Midjourney / Ideogram to create a small set of custom pieces: icon, logo, 1–2 hero illustrations, 1 special button.  
> Use negative prompts to kill the generic look: “no glossy, no corporate, no 3D gradients.”  
> Clean them up (remove background, tweak colors) so they’re Figma‑ready.

1–3 strong custom elements beat 20 random assets.

5/ Assemble in Figma like a real app

> Drop assets into real iOS / Android frames.  
> Stick to an 8px grid, 2 fonts max, one accent color.  
> Use blend modes and overlays so the AI art actually matches your background and type.

Now you have a legit, high‑fidelity design, not a screenshot from a model.

6/ Re‑vibe code the app

> Feed the final Figma screens + exported assets back into Google AI Studio or Claude Code.  
> Tell it: “Rebuild the existing prototype using this layout, colors, and assets only.”  
> Iterate until the code matches the design.

2113534175479255099.name: mr.sky | AI & Last News
2113534175479255099.text:
Ideogram launches Vector 1.0 AI SVG editor

It’s time to dive into some fresh AI tech that could shake up your design workflow. Ideogram has just launched Vector 1.0, an innovative tool for generating scalable vector graphics (SVGs) from text prompts or existing images.

So, what exactly is new here? Well, the standout feature of Vector 1.0 is its ability to edit individual elements within generated SVG files. You can move, rotate, scale, and recolor shapes independently—basically giving you a fully editable file that’s not just static but customizable as needed. This means no more starting from scratch with vector editors like Adobe Illustrator; instead, you get close to your desired result quickly and then refine it.

But why should you care? If you’re in design or marketing, this could save you hours of manual work. For developers, the API access makes integrating vector generation into apps and services a breeze. So, how does Vector 1.0 actually work?

Vector 1.0 uses AI models trained on vast datasets of SVG files and text descriptions. When you input a prompt, the model generates an SVG file that matches your description as closely as possible. The same goes for converting raster images—Vector 1.0 analyzes the image and translates it into scalable vector format.

Now, let’s talk numbers. Ideogram says their API pricing starts at $0.13 per generation without references and can go up to $0.32 with high-quality results that use reference images. Converting an existing raster image costs $0.10. But there are limitations—automatic layering of shapes into groups isn’t yet implemented, which means you might have to manually organize elements in your design software afterward.

class Adaptive_Timeline_Artifact:

    def __init__(self):
        self.accuracy_search: "TRUE" 
        self.subject = "{$SUBJECT}"
        self.time_range = "[OPTIONAL START / END DATE or AI_INFER]"
        self.milestone_count = "[OPTIONAL or AI_INFER]"

        self.parents = {

            "museum_parent":
                "Luxury historical exhibition display — museum object photography, archival elegance, tactile artifacts, restrained labels, curated chronology",

            "timeline_parent":
                "Physical chronology made spatial — milestone objects arranged along one continuous visual journey rather than a conventional horizontal infographic",

            "editorial_parent":
                "Elegant historical publication — oversized serif title, fine date labels, concise captions, sophisticated negative space",

            "diorama_parent":
                "Miniature 3D artifact collection — physically believable objects, handcrafted scale, soft cast shadows, rich materials, collector-display precision",

            "metaphor_parent":
                "The overall path geometry is semantically inferred from the subject rather than fixed"
        }

        self.mutations = {

            "layout_mutation":
                """
                AI_INFER the most meaningful spatial metaphor for {$SUBJECT}.

                Possible structures include but are not limited to:

                sound / music          -> waveform, acoustic arc, groove, spiral
                aviation              -> ascending flight trajectory
                space exploration     -> orbital path / expanding solar system
                transportation        -> road, rail, route map, switchback
                computing             -> circuit trace / branching network
                communication         -> signal wave / connected nodes
                architecture          -> evolving skyline
                art history           -> gallery wall / brushstroke ribbon
                biology               -> evolutionary tree / DNA helix
                medicine              -> anatomical pathway / pulse line
                fashion               -> flowing fabric ribbon / runway
                cinema                -> film strip / projection beam
                photography           -> aperture spiral / film reel
                weapons               -> ballistic trajectory / arsenal progression
                literature            -> unfolding pages / bookshelf chronology
                philosophy            -> branching argument tree / concentric thought rings
                food                  -> recipe chain / ingredient transformation
                energy                -> power-flow diagram
                ocean exploration     -> descending depth profile
                mountain history      -> ascending elevation profile
                civilization          -> river / road / layered archaeological strata

                Do NOT choose these mechanically.
                Infer a fresh spatial metaphor from the subject's actual semantic structure.
                """,

            "object_mutation":
                """
                AI_INFER the landmark artifacts, inventions, people, organisms,
                buildings, tools, vehicles, devices, cultural objects,
                discoveries, symbols, or turning points that best represent
                the evolution of {$SUBJECT}.
                """,

            "chronology_mutation":
                """
                Allocate spatial distance according to historical significance,
                not merely equal year intervals.
                Major transitions receive more visual emphasis.
                Quiet transitional periods may compress.
                """,

            "artifact_mutation":
                """
                Render each milestone as a miniature physical artifact,
                model, sculptural icon, specimen, or environmental fragment
                appropriate to the subject.
                Avoid reducing everything to flat icons.
                """,

            "annotation_mutation":
                """
                Generate date / era,
                short milestone name,
                optional one-line descriptor,
                inventor / creator / location / event where relevant.
                Keep labels restrained and museum-like.
                """,

            "origin_mutation":
                """
                AI_INFER a meaningful visual origin artifact.
                This may be:
                an opened archive box,
                excavation case,
                antique book,
                workshop drawer,
                specimen cabinet,
                instrument case,
                shipping crate,
                map case,
                laboratory tray,
                or another subject-appropriate container.
                """,

            "future_mutation":
                """
                The final milestones may subtly change in material,
                scale, illumination, or abstraction to suggest the present
                and possible future without turning into science-fiction clutter.
                """
        }

    def generate(self):

        HISTORY = AI_INFER(
            historically_significant_milestones(
                subject=self.subject,
                range=self.time_range,
                count=self.milestone_count
            )
        )

        PATH = AI_INFER(
            spatial_metaphor(
                subject=self.subject,
                history=HISTORY,
                rule="shape must communicate the nature of the subject"
            )
        )

        ORIGIN = AI_INFER(
            archival_origin_object(
                subject=self.subject,
                first_milestone=HISTORY[0]
            )
        )

        return render(

            subject = """
            Create a single luxurious visual history of {$SUBJECT}.

            Do not use a generic straight timeline.

            Transform the chronology itself into a physical sculptural path
            whose shape is inferred from the meaning, mechanics, culture,
            or behavior of {$SUBJECT}.

            Arrange historically meaningful miniature artifacts along this path.

            Every milestone should be visually recognizable first
            and labeled second.

            The viewer should understand the evolution of the subject
            even before reading the annotations.
            """,

            layout = PATH,

            origin = ORIGIN,

            artifacts = """
            8–20 AI-inferred milestones.
            Each rendered as an elegant miniature object or sculptural vignette.
            Vary scale according to historical importance.
            Preserve realistic differences in materials between eras.
            """,

            typography = """
            Large elegant serif title:
            AI_INFER poetic historical title from {$SUBJECT}

            Optional date range beneath title.

            Milestones:
            DATE / ERA
            concise milestone name
            optional micro-caption
            """,

            environment = """
            Warm neutral museum wall or archival paper-like surface.
            Vast breathing room.
            Timeline objects cast subtle physical shadows.
            No conventional infographic boxes.
            """,

            lighting = """
            Museum-display lighting,
            warm directional illumination,
            gentle falloff,
            restrained highlights,
            rich material realism,
            subtle vignette only from natural light falloff.
            """,

            rendering = """
            premium 3D object photography,
            historical artifact realism,
            editorial museum design,
            finely modeled miniature details,
            physically plausible materials,
            elegant depth,
            8K.
            """,

            constraints = """
            No generic equal-spacing timeline.
            No repetitive iconography.
            No random milestones.
            No visually identical objects.
            No single fixed layout applied to every topic.
            Layout MUST emerge from {$SUBJECT}.
            """
        )

👇prompt

@画像を作成する

OUTPUT_ASPECT_RATIO = "4:5"
OUTPUT_LANGUAGE = "AUTO"
FIGURE_COUNT = "1 or 2"
COPY_AMOUNT = "MEDIUM"
DOODLE_DENSITY = "HIGH"
EDITORIAL_LEVEL = "VERY HIGH"
STYLE_MODE = "PHOTO_X_HANDDRAWN_NOTE_EDITORIAL"

You are a world-class creative director, art director, editorial designer, fashion photographer, stylist, illustrator, hand-lettering artist, typographer, brand designer, and marketer.

Read the attached screenshots, profiles, posts, URLs, text, photographs, illustrations, products, and brand information. Extract their essential theme, personality, emotional appeal, audience, value, colors, and symbolic motifs.

Do not reproduce the original UI, layout, advertisement, magazine cover, illustration style, or brand design. Transform the source into one completely original editorial advertising image in OUTPUT_ASPECT_RATIO.

If a URL cannot be verified, prioritize the attached images and text. Never invent unknown facts.

Do not output questions, analysis, explanations, or production notes. Generate only the finished image.

Core concept:

Create a pop and intimate editorial visual in which a real fashion model represents reality, while hand-drawn typography and illustrations visualize the person’s thoughts, interests, emotions, memories, possibilities, and brand world.

The result should feel like a fusion of:

- fashion editorial photography
- a culture magazine opening page
- a personal sketchbook
- a handwritten campaign poster
- an intelligently edited doodle notebook

It must not feel like a portrait with decorations added afterward. The photograph, lettering, drawings, symbols, and negative space must belong to the same world.

The goal is to make viewers feel:

“interesting”
“stylish”
“I want to look closer”
“I want to save this”
“I understand this person’s world”

Internal interpretation:

From the input, determine:

- the central theme
- the target audience
- the strongest emotional appeal
- the personality of the person, product, or brand
- the most important message
- one dominant visual color
- suitable fashion styling
- meaningful objects, tools, places, hobbies, emotions, and future possibilities
- short words or phrases that can become hand lettering
- motifs that can become simple line drawings

Do not include everything. Select one central story and build a coherent visual world around it.

Main figure:

Even when the source material is a screenshot, text, illustration, character, animal, or product, use one or two realistic fictional East Asian fashion models as the main visual subject unless the input clearly requires the original product itself.

The person must appear as a professionally photographed editorial model, isolated from the original environment and placed on a clean paper-like background.

Use:

- natural skin, eyes, hair, hands, and body structure
- a full-body or near-full-body composition
- a distinctive but relaxed expression
- a pose with an interesting silhouette
- a slight turn, lean, seated pose, hand gesture, or asymmetrical body angle
- natural interaction with a relevant object when useful
- a subtle contact shadow so the figure feels physically present on the page

Avoid:

- stiff front-facing poses
- generic smiling business portraits
- pointing, thumbs-up, crossed arms, or exaggerated gestures
- cheap stock-photo expressions
- artificial AI beauty
- excessive skin retouching
- environmental office or studio backgrounds

Fashion styling:

The outfit must function as the largest color shape in the composition.

Create urban, playful, contemporary fashion that has personality but still feels wearable.

Use elements such as:

- one vivid dress, shirt, knit, jacket, skirt, or set-up
- clean silhouettes with a slightly unusual detail
- stripes, checks, pleats, geometric patterns, or color blocking
- stylish glasses
- designed shoes, socks, bags, jewelry, or accessories
- a hairstyle that strengthens the silhouette
- colors derived from the source material

Do not use ordinary businesswear, bland casual clothing, mass-market office styling, cosplay, theatrical costumes, oversized frills, or excessive runway fashion.

Background and composition:

Use a white, warm-white, or very pale paper-like background as the visual stage.

Do not use a full photographic location or a large saturated background color field.

The figure should occupy approximately 40–65% of the frame and become the dominant photographic and color anchor.

Arrange the figure slightly off-center when appropriate, leaving active drawing space around the head, shoulders, hands, and body silhouette.

Build the composition with:

1. one realistic cutout fashion figure or two interacting figures
2. one large hand-drawn headline
3. several smaller handwritten words or short labels
4. meaningful black-line illustrations
5. small symbols, arrows, frames, ribbons, dotted paths, or radiating lines
6. limited pastel or accent-color fills
7. visible white space connecting all elements

The page may be dense, but it must not be filled evenly. Create rhythm through:

dense area → breathing space → dense area

The eye should move in this order:

face → main headline → body or held object → surrounding discoveries

Hand-drawn illustrations:

This is one of the most important elements.

Surround and partially overlap the model with hand-drawn illustrations derived from the source content.

Possible motifs include:

- tools and work objects
- fashion items
- food or products
- travel, cities, transport, landscapes, or buildings
- technology, computers, devices, or interfaces simplified into drawings
- hobbies, music, books, art materials, or daily objects
- emotions, conversations, discoveries, dreams, and future possibilities
- small characters, faces, animals, symbols, or humorous imaginary creatures

Every major drawing must relate to the input theme, personality, value, or story.

Use mostly thin to medium black or dark-gray linework with small areas of the main color and one or two supporting colors.

The shapes may have subtle handmade irregularity, but every contour must remain clean, deliberate, complete, and visually separated.

Handmade must never mean dirty, damaged, tangled, scribbled, unfinished, or visually broken.

Prefer fewer, clearer, more readable illustrations over many tiny or repetitive drawings.

Do not create visual density by repeating the same character, mascot, animal, face, icon, product, or symbolic motif many times.

If the input contains or strongly suggests a recurring mascot, avatar, character, animal, icon, or symbolic figure:

- create one simple canonical design
- keep its silhouette, proportions, facial structure, markings, and line weight consistent
- use it only when it carries clear meaning
- show no more than one to three appearances of the same recurring design in the entire image
- do not use it as an all-over pattern or repeated filler
- vary only the pose or expression slightly
- if it is not essential to the central story, use it once or omit it

Do not invent a recurring mascot when the input does not justify one.

When an illustration appears on a small surface such as a laptop, product, package, label, sticker, badge, card, accessory, or screen:

- simplify it into one flat and front-facing icon
- use minimal facial or internal details
- preserve a clear outer silhouette
- keep a clean margin around the icon
- do not add handwriting, decorative strokes, textures, or nearby marks inside the small surface
- omit the illustration if it would be too small to remain clean and recognizable

Keep a small clear-space margin around every character, face, mascot, product icon, or detailed symbolic drawing.

Do not let arrows, stars, rays, dotted paths, lettering, frames, or unrelated decorative lines cross through or visually merge with:

- faces
- eyes
- mouths
- bodies
- hands
- products
- logos
- stickers
- readable text

Strictly avoid:

- stray or floating lines
- accidental black marks
- dirty smudges
- tangled contours
- doubled or broken outlines
- unfinished drawing fragments
- duplicated facial features
- extra eyes, ears, limbs, fingers, tails, or facial marks
- black scribbled patches
- unrelated lines touching a character
- decorative marks that look like damage or printing errors

The drawings must not look like:

- children’s worksheets
- school festival decoration
- generic clip art
- sticker packs
- kawaii stationery
- meaningless stars, hearts, arrows, and clouds
- unrelated objects added only to fill space

The illustrations must interact with the model by following the body contour, emerging from gestures, framing the face, connecting to an object, passing behind the figure, or extending the person’s thoughts into the surrounding space.

Typography and hand lettering:

Use OUTPUT_LANGUAGE for all important readable copy.

When OUTPUT_LANGUAGE is not English, small English accents may be included. When OUTPUT_LANGUAGE is English, keep all major copy in English.

Use:

- one large main headline
- four to ten short supporting words or micro-phrases
- an optional brand, issue, campaign, season, or project name
- no long explanatory paragraphs

The main headline should be hand-lettered and visually expressive, not plain typeset text.

Mix a controlled range of lettering styles according to function:

- rounded outlined lettering
- hand-drawn block capitals
- condensed serif lettering
- casual handwritten notes
- decorative script
- ribbon or banner lettering
- slightly irregular vertical or curved arrangements

Do not give every phrase equal visual strength.

Use the hierarchy:

one large title
two or three medium phrases
several small discoveries

Letters may curve, tilt, stack, follow an illustration, sit inside a ribbon, overlap the figure slightly, or align with the body silhouette.

All visible words must be correctly spelled and semantically connected to the source. Do not use meaningless English or broken text.

Color:

Use a restrained paper-based palette:

- white or warm white as the largest area
- black or dark gray for linework and information structure
- one dominant accent color taken from the source
- one or two soft supporting colors
- optional tiny areas of pale yellow, pink, blue, green, or another matching color

The model’s clothing should carry the largest accent-color area.

Repeat that color in selected lettering, lines, icons, or illustrations so the photograph and drawings feel connected.

Do not use every color at equal strength.

Avoid muddy colors, brownish filters, heavy gray, full-black areas, rainbow palettes, random neon colors, and overly sweet pastel decoration.

Information density:

Create rich but controlled discovery density without using long text.

Use a limited selection of clear visual discoveries such as:

- short words
- tiny labels
- symbolic objects
- diagrams
- miniature scenes
- a small number of characters
- dotted paths
- stars, rays, or motion lines used only when meaningful

Do not increase density by shrinking illustrations until they become unclear or by repeating the same motif many times.

Use stars, rays, arrows, dotted paths, and motion lines sparingly and only in open background areas.

From a distance, the viewer should see one clear person and one clear headline.

Up close, the viewer should discover a richer personal or brand story.

Mood:

Bright, curious, youthful, intelligent, personal, playful, approachable, and slightly nostalgic.

The visual should feel handcrafted but not amateur.

It should communicate personality and culture rather than aggressively selling a product.

Avoid:

- giant heavy logo typography dominating the full page
- strong full-bleed color backgrounds
- conventional advertising banners
- generic portrait plus surrounding icons
- ordinary photo plus decorative doodles
- Canva or template layouts
- infographic or educational poster layouts
- equal spacing between every element
- symmetrical decoration around the figure
- random handwritten words
- excessive speech bubbles
- flat sticker-like illustrations
- childish or overly cute drawing styles
- repeated use of the same mascot or character
- tiny drawings with unclear shapes
- dirty or accidental-looking linework
- dark backgrounds
- ordinary office photography
- long copy
- tiny unreadable paragraphs
- copying an existing magazine, advertisement, illustrator, or brand

Final internal check:

Before generating, verify:

- Is the white paper-like background clearly visible?
- Is the real model the first visual focus?
- Does the outfit create one strong color anchor?
- Does the model’s silhouette create an interesting graphic shape?
- Is there one clear hand-lettered headline?
- Are the surrounding words visually subordinate to the headline?
- Are the illustrations derived from the source rather than generic decoration?
- Do the photographs, lettering, and drawings physically interact?
- Is the page dense without being evenly filled?
- Are repeated characters or motifs limited to one to three meaningful appearances?
- Is every small icon or character large enough to remain recognizable?
- Are all contours clean, complete, and free from stray marks?
- Are faces, products, stickers, and readable words protected from crossing decorative lines?
- Does it feel like an edited sketchbook rather than a children’s worksheet?
- Is it clear from far away and rewarding from close up?
- Does it feel personal, collectible, and save-worthy?

If any part feels generic, childish, repetitive, dirty, disconnected, or visually flat, redesign the composition, hierarchy, motif count, line cleanliness, and color repetition internally before generating.

Final output:

Generate one high-resolution image in OUTPUT_ASPECT_RATIO.

Use a clean white paper-like background.
Use one or two realistic fashion models.
Use one dominant clothing color.
Use integrated hand lettering and meaningful line drawings.
Use recurring characters or motifs sparingly and consistently.
Keep all linework clean, deliberate, and free from accidental visual noise.
Create a high-density editorial page with a clear hierarchy.
Prioritize personality, discovery, and emotional storytelling over explanation.
Make it completely original.

Do not display analysis, explanation, production notes, or the prompt itself.

Input materials:

Refer to every image, screenshot, URL, text, photograph, illustration, product, and brand detail attached to this message.

× contemporary editorial vector art

SEMANTIC INFERENCE

AUTHENTIC MICRO-TEXT

street signs

transit signs
labels
dates
mission names
product names
technical markings
historical locations

meaningless text

VISUAL STYLE

subtle paper grain
