SEO Lead will coordinate the work and approvals.

🔎 1. AUDIT OUR EXISTING CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE

Map what happens from confirmed purchase through successful delivery.

Identify:

• Purchase confirmation.

• Welcome process.

• Client information requests.

• Required account permissions.

• Project setup.

• Work milestones.

• Progress updates.

• Testing.

• Delivery.

• Customer training.

• Post-delivery support.

• Renewal or repeat-purchase opportunities.

• Existing referral processes.

Use actual business records and approved policies.

Identify missing steps, repeated requests, unclear responsibilities, and common delays.

Do not recreate working systems unnecessarily.

🚨 2. FIND THE TEN MOST LIKELY CUSTOMER PROBLEMS

Analyze authorized:

• Support inquiries.

• Customer questions.

• Previous project delays.

• Complaints.

• Missing information requests.

• Failed handoffs.

• Refund or cancellation reasons.

• Common setup mistakes.

• Customer feedback.

• Frequently repeated questions.

Identify up to TEN meaningful problems.

For each, record:

• Likely cause.

• Evidence.

• Effect on the customer.

• Effect on our business.

• Likelihood, where supportable.

• Severity.

• Preventive action.

• How the system will detect failure.

• Responsible specialist.

Rank problems by customer harm, frequency, and ease of prevention.

Don't invent incident rates.

📚 3. CREATE A PREVENTIVE SOP LIBRARY

Build SOPs for the important processes.

Each SOP must include:

Process name.

Purpose.

Trigger.

Required information.

Required access.

Responsible owner.

Exact steps.

Expected output.

Verification checklist.

Common exceptions.

Recovery instructions.

Approval requirements.

Source documents.

Last review date.

Create SOPs for:

• Customer onboarding.

• Collecting project information.

• Verifying account access.

• Project readiness.

• Progress updates.

• Scope-change requests.

• Customer support.

• Final testing.

• Customer handoff.

• Post-delivery follow-up.

Use our real approved business procedures.

📁 4. BUILD A SINGLE CLIENT INTAKE SYSTEM

Create a simple form or portal through our existing software where supported.

Collect only the information required for the purchased service.

For a digital marketing agency, consider:

• Business contact information.

• Approved services and offers.

• Branding.

• Website and domain information.

• Required assets.

• Customer FAQs.

• Booking preferences.

• Business hours, where relevant.

• Existing software.

• Authorized account-access instructions.

• Project decisions.

• Final approval requirements.

Use conditional fields where supported.

A conditional field appears only when a previous answer makes it relevant.

Provide examples of acceptable answers.

Make required fields clear.

Allow customers to save progress where the platform supports it.

Do not collect passwords in ordinary form fields or email.

Use secure invitations or approved credential tools.

✅ 5. BUILD THE PROJECT READINESS CHECKLIST

Before declaring a project ready, verify the actual requirements.

Examples:

• Payment confirmed.

• Intake completed.

• Required assets received.

• Account permissions verified.

• Offer details approved.

• Project scope confirmed.

• Start conditions satisfied.

• Delivery schedule established.

For each requirement, record:

COMPLETE / MISSING / NEEDS REVIEW.

Clearly separate missing client inputs from unfinished business tasks.

Use the actual contract to determine when the delivery period begins.

Never invent a delivery guarantee.

👋 6. CREATE A COMPLETE CUSTOMER WELCOME PACKAGE

Prepare:

A. Welcome email.

B. One-page getting-started guide.

C. Client intake link.

D. Required materials checklist.

E. Secure access instructions.

F. Delivery process explanation.

G. Milestone schedule.

H. Support contact information.

I. FAQ section.

J. Next-step confirmation.

Write at a simple reading level.

Use short sentences and clear instructions.

Explain exactly what the customer needs to do first.

Avoid asking customers to interpret complicated technical instructions.

📅 7. BUILD USEFUL CUSTOMER STATUS UPDATES

Create status messages for:

• Purchase confirmed.

• Intake incomplete.

• Intake completed.

• Project ready to begin.

• Work started.

• Milestone completed.

• Approval required.

• Testing underway.

• Project completed.

• Training or handoff ready.

For each message, explain:

• What has been completed.

• What's happening next.

• Whether customer action is required.

• The exact next step.

• The relevant timeline, if verified.

Use native platform triggers where practical.

Prevent duplicate or outdated updates.

🧠 8. BUILD THE CUSTOMER SUPPORT KNOWLEDGE BASE

Organize information into THREE layers.

LAYER A: GENERAL BUSINESS INFORMATION

Policies, services, support hours, and general FAQs.

LAYER B: PRODUCT OR SERVICE KNOWLEDGE

Approved packages, delivery steps, features, and troubleshooting instructions.

LAYER C: CUSTOMER-SPECIFIC INFORMATION

Authorized project status, purchased package, milestones, and relevant customer records.

Apply proper access controls.

Never reveal one customer's information to another.

Keep passwords, payment secrets, and unnecessary sensitive data out of ordinary knowledge documents.

Use current approved information as the source of truth.

Flag conflicts or missing information.

✍️ 9. TRAIN OUR BUSINESS COMMUNICATION STYLE

Analyze up to TEN approved examples of our own customer emails or support replies.

Extract:

• Tone.

• Greeting style.

• Sentence length.

• Common phrases.

• Explanation style.

• Level of detail.

• How concerns are acknowledged.

• How next steps are presented.

• Closing style.

Create:

BUSINESS CUSTOMER COMMUNICATION STYLE GUIDE.

Draft FIVE sample replies for common situations.

Compare the drafts with our actual writing examples.

Revise the guide based on owner feedback.

Do not imitate a specific person deceptively.

Do not claim a human personally completed an action unless verified.

🟢 10. CREATE SUPPORT RESPONSE LEVELS

Create three groups.

GREEN: APPROVED ROUTINE RESPONSES

Use verified knowledge-base answers.

Only automate responses through tools and workflows authorized for sending.

YELLOW: REQUIRES REVIEW

Research the answer.

Prepare a helpful draft.

Flag the exact question requiring verification.

RED: HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED

Flag sensitive or consequential issues.

Prepare a concise internal summary.

Identify the relevant policy or record.

Provide the responsible person with a suggested response and necessary context.

Do not issue unauthorized refunds, change contracts, promise compensation, or disclose confidential information.

Do not falsely imply that a human authored an automated message.

Answer accurately if a customer asks whether AI is involved.

📨 11. CONNECT CUSTOMER SUPPORT CHANNELS

Use our authorized inbox, ticketing platform, CRM, and knowledge base.

Determine which existing platform features can:

• Identify incoming support requests.

• Find the correct customer record.

• Categorize the issue.

• Retrieve relevant approved information.

• Prepare accurate replies.

• Route exceptions.

• Record outcomes.

Where appropriate, create native platform rules for approved low-risk replies.

If Grok Bot itself handles messages through browser or email tools, respect the platform's required sending approvals.

Test every supported integration before activation.

🧪 12. TEST REALISTIC CUSTOMER SITUATIONS

Use safe test records.

Test at least:

• New customer purchase.

• Missing project materials.

• Incomplete intake.

• Incorrect access.

• Conflicting project instructions.

• Customer asks about delivery timing.

• Customer requests a package change.

• Customer reports a defect.

• Customer requests a refund.

• Customer complains angrily.

• Customer asks for a human.

• Customer asks whether the reply is automated.

• Customer requests another customer's information.

Verify the correct knowledge source, response, permission, and next step.

Fix errors before enabling routine automation.

🛠️ 13. IMPLEMENT APPROVED CUSTOMER WORKFLOWS

Use our existing software.

Prepare related improvements in batches.

Where supported, implement:

• Welcome package delivery.

• Client intake forms.

• Required-materials tracking.

• Project readiness checks.

• Milestone updates.

• Support categorization.

• Approved routine responses.

• Exception alerts.

• Customer training and handoff.

• Follow-up checks.

Request approval before sending new live customer communications or changing consequential business processes.

Verify every completed action.

📈 14. CREATE A PROACTIVE CUSTOMER HEALTH CHECK

Use the actual project and support records to identify warning signs.

Examples:

• Onboarding not completed.

• Required information still missing.

• Missed project milestone.

• Repeated support requests.

• Unresolved complaint.

• Customer unable to use the delivered system.

• A previously working feature failing.

Create a short risk report.

For each customer issue, record:

• Verified problem.

• Supporting evidence.

• Customer impact.

• Recommended preventive action.

• Assigned owner.

• Required response date.

Do not label a customer as unhappy or likely to leave without adequate evidence.

Use native event alerts for urgent failures.

Recommend a limited Grok Bot review schedule for nonurgent problems.

🎓 15. MAKE THE FINAL HANDOFF EASY

Before closing a project, prepare:

• Delivery checklist.

• Working links.

• Completed features.

• Important account access instructions.

• Short user guide.

• Relevant tutorial videos or screenshots.

• Maintenance responsibilities.

• Support contact details.

• Known limitations.

• Approved next steps.

Verify that the customer can use the system.

Don't assume project completion means the customer understands what was delivered.

❤️ 16. FOLLOW UP AFTER DELIVERY

Create a useful post-delivery check.

Ask:

• Is the product or system working?

• Can the customer complete the main task?

• Are any instructions unclear?

• Has an important problem appeared?

• Is additional help needed?

Offer a relevant solution when appropriate.

Record genuine feedback.

Don't immediately turn every support conversation into an upsell.

🔁 17. IDENTIFY REPEAT-CUSTOMER OPPORTUNITIES

Review products and services that could genuinely help an existing customer.

Examples:

• Maintenance.

• Updates.

• Additional training.

• A relevant new service.

• A compatible product.

• A support package.

Recommend an offer only when it matches a demonstrated customer need.

Use actual customer records and approved marketing permissions.

Do not invent buying needs.

🤝 18. BUILD A GENUINE REFERRAL PROCESS

First, determine whether the customer received the promised service and has a reasonable opportunity to evaluate it.

Where appropriate, prepare a simple voluntary referral invitation.

Include:

• The type of customer our business can help.

• A simple sharing link or introduction method.

• What the referred person can expect.

• Any real referral terms.

• An easy way to decline.

If referral rewards are offered, verify their eligibility, disclosure, and legal requirements.

Keep referrals separate from public review requests.

Do not pay for favorable reviews or condition review incentives on positive sentiment.

Do not use fake testimonials.

Do not pressure customers with unresolved problems to recommend the business.

📊 19. MEASURE THE CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE

Create a CUSTOMER SUCCESS SCOREBOARD.

Track available:

• Onboarding completion rate.

• Time to first useful result.

• Missing-information delays.

• Number of repeated information requests.

• Support response time.

• Reopened support issues.

• Project delivery reliability.

• Customer effort feedback.

• Repeat purchases.

• Renewals.

• Voluntary referrals.

• Referral customers.

• Cancellations and refunds.

Customer Effort Score is a measure of how easy or difficult customers found an interaction.

Where appropriate, use a simple question such as:

'How easy was it to get started with our service?'

Measure using a consistent scale.

Record actual results and sample size.

Do not invent satisfaction rates.

🔁 20. SAVE REUSABLE CUSTOMER SUCCESS SKILLS

After testing the processes, create reusable Skills.

Suggested names:

CUSTOMER ONBOARDING.

PROJECT READINESS CHECK.

CUSTOMER SUPPORT RESPONSE.

PROJECT STATUS UPDATE.

CUSTOMER HANDOFF.

CUSTOMER HEALTH REVIEW.

REFERRAL INVITATION.

Each Skill must contain:

• Trigger.

• Required information.

• Exact steps.

• Source of truth.

• Approval boundaries.

• Verification method.

• Error handling.

• Completion criteria.

Use native software automation for immediate events.

Use Grok Bot Routines for narrow, scheduled work when beneficial.

Avoid unnecessary frequent checks and repeated Bot conversations.

📁 21. CREATE THE COMPLETE CUSTOMER SUCCESS SYSTEM

Deliver:

CUSTOMER SUCCESS & RETENTION PLAYBOOK - [BUSINESS NAME]

Include:

Customer journey map.

Preventable problem report.

SOP library.

Client intake system.

Project readiness checklist.

Welcome package.

Progress update templates.

Knowledge-base structure.

Business communication style guide.

Support response levels.

Approved automation workflows.

Human-review rules.

Complete test results.

Customer handoff materials.

Customer health monitoring.

Repeat-purchase opportunities.

Referral process.

Customer Success Scoreboard.

Reusable Skills.

Completed changes and remaining decisions.

Request one consolidated implementation approval before activating consequential customer-facing changes.

Complete the authorized work.

Verify live functionality.

Deliver the completed system and report.

Stop after the assigned work is finished."

✅ END OF PROMPT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🚀 STEP 10: WHAT THIS LOOKS LIKE FOR AN ACTUAL BUSINESS

Imagine a customer purchases your approved website automation package.

Instead of waiting for a series of confusing emails, they immediately receive:

✅ A clear welcome message.

✅ One organized intake link.

✅ A list of required materials.

✅ Instructions for secure account access.

✅ A checklist showing what's complete.

✅ A clear explanation of when the project begins.

Your Grok Bot helps verify readiness.

The existing project system handles routine status notifications.

And when the customer asks a question, the support system checks the relevant approved information.

If the question is routine, it follows the authorized response process.

If the answer requires judgment, the Bot prepares the research and alerts the responsible person.

The customer gets fewer surprises.

The business experiences fewer preventable delays.

And both sides spend less time repeating the same information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🤝 STEP 11: WHY REFERRALS BELONG IN CUSTOMER SUCCESS

Here's an important distinction.

A referral program doesn't automatically make customers happy.

A discount for telling someone about your business won't repair a broken service.

But a good customer experience gives people something worth recommending.

Think about Chewy again.

The customer didn't share that story because she was promised a referral commission.

She shared it because the experience mattered to her.

The experience created the reason to talk.

The referral opportunity simply makes it easier for customers who want to recommend a business to do so.

And recommendations can also matter for businesses offering services people rarely purchase twice.

A roofing customer may not need another roof soon.

But they may know several neighbors who do.

Satisfied customers can help a business grow through repeat purchases, genuine recommendations, or both.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 STEP 12: BUILD A BUSINESS THAT GETS EASIER TO RUN

Your support system should improve every time it encounters a preventable problem.

If three customers struggle with the same setup instruction:

Improve the instruction.

If customers repeatedly ask where to upload their logo:

Make the upload link easier to find.

If project deadlines are delayed by missing access:

Improve the access checklist.

If customers don't understand how to use the finished product:

Improve the handoff guide.

Don't just answer the same support question forever.

Fix the process that keeps creating the question.

That's the biggest lightbulb moment in this entire chapter.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 THE TAKEAWAY

Getting the first sale is important.

But what happens AFTER the sale determines whether the customer receives the value they expected.

Your Grok Bot team can help you:

Predict common problems.

Create preventive SOPs.

Simplify onboarding.

Collect everything needed in one organized process.

Provide useful progress updates.

Answer routine questions accurately.

Recognize when human judgment is needed.

Deliver better handoffs.

Identify genuine repeat-purchase opportunities.

And make it easier for satisfied customers to recommend your business.

Don't build a support system that only reacts to problems.

Build a customer success system that prevents as many problems as possible.

Because the easiest support problem to solve is the one your customer never has to experience.

NEXT: Turn your customer feedback, support questions, and project results into improvements your Grok Bots can make across your entire business. 🔄

Market volume is still pretty weak, so I'll probably be posting fewer recaps for a while. I don't think there's any reason to force trades every day, especially when liquidity is this fragmented.

And the last token I want to cover today is $DARK 

This one actually launched over a month ago, but quite a few people have been asking me about it recently. I didn't pay much attention to it at first, but after spending some time researching the product, tokenomics, revenue, and what the team has built so far, I found a few things worth discussing

I'll go through both the positives and the risks that I think everyone should be aware of

1. What is Darkwoods actually building?

Darkwoods is a privacy-first AI platform

The idea is pretty straightforward. Instead of jumping between different platforms for different tasks, users can access multiple AI tools within a single ecosystem

The platform currently offers LLM chat, image and video generation, audio tools, coding assistance through DarkCode, and several other creative features

What they're trying to differentiate themselves with is privacy

According to the team, Darkwoods uses Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) for certain workloads, along with anonymous AI access and a no-prompt-logging policy

However, I think it's important to separate what the team claims from what's actually been independently verified. So far, I haven't seen a comprehensive independent audit confirming all of their privacy claims

Another thing I find interesting is their approach to building the product

Instead of spending years developing their own AI models from scratch, they're integrating existing models from providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, then building their own user experience and privacy layer on top

This allows them to ship much faster, although it also means they're still heavily dependent on third-party infrastructure

2. Their development speed has been pretty impressive

This is probably what caught my attention the most

In just over a month, the team has continued shipping new features, going from basic AI chat to image generation, video tools, coding, and more advanced creative workflows

Some notable recent updates :

> October 13 : ElevenLabs integration for voice features
> October 15 : Added Nano Banana 2.1
> October 16 : Integrated Krea 3 for image editing
> October 20 : Launched Director Mode

Out of these, Director Mode is probably the most interesting feature to me

Instead of generating images, videos, and audio separately and putting everything together manually, users can start with a single idea and let the platform help handle the creative workflow, from scripts and storyboards to video and sound

If they execute this well, it could become one of the features that attracts users beyond the crypto community

That said, I don't want to overvalue a project simply because it's shipping updates quickly

Shipping fast is a good sign, but what really matters is whether people actually keep using the product

3. Tokenomics – What makes $DARK different from many other AI tokens?

One thing I like about Darkwoods is that they're trying to connect actual business activity to the token

Users don't need to hold $DARK to access the platform. Instead, they purchase credits using stablecoins or other supported cryptocurrencies

According to the team's published model, credit revenue is distributed as follows :

> 10% goes toward $DARK buybacks and burns
> 10% goes toward staking rewards, paid in USDG
> 80% goes toward operating expenses and AI inference costs

The model is pretty easy to understand

If more people use the platform and purchase credits, the amount allocated to buybacks and staking rewards could increase as well

What I particularly like is that staking rewards are paid in stablecoins rather than newly issued $DARK tokens. That means staking rewards don't directly create additional token inflation

The team also claims that $DARK had a 100% community launch, with no dedicated team allocation.

However, a community launch doesn't automatically mean the supply is well distributed. We still need to examine early buyers, connected wallets, and how concentrated the current holder distribution actually is

Another thing worth mentioning is that the revenue allocation percentages can be modified through contract administration, so the 10/10/80 structure shouldn't be treated as permanently fixed

And of course, buybacks don't guarantee price appreciation. Their actual impact depends on how much is being bought relative to the selling pressure in the market

4. What do the revenue numbers actually look like?

This is probably the part I'm most interested in

Having an AI product is one thing. Getting people to actually pay for it is another

Based on the data collected as of October 23 :

Darkwoods has reportedly generated around $51,301 USDG in cumulative credit revenue, crossing the $50K milestone in less than its first 30 days

A few other numbers worth mentioning :

> Around 16.47M $DARK tokens have been burned
> The team announced an additional $10,000 allocation from creator fees for token buybacks
> Approximately 25.74M $DARK is currently staked
> There are 37 staking wallets
> Total staking rewards distributed are around $4,705 USDG

I think the fact that the project has reported revenue and already has mechanisms connecting that revenue to the token is worth paying attention to

But there's something important here

That $51K is reported cumulative revenue, not net profit, and it shouldn't automatically be treated as $51K in recurring monthly revenue

According to the available data, credit purchases over the most recent 24 hours were only around $196

That's significantly below the daily average you'd get by dividing $51K by 30 days

It raises an important question: did most of the early revenue come from a few large credit purchases, promotional campaigns, or actual recurring demand?

Personally, I'd rather watch another 2–4 weeks of revenue data before making any assumptions about the project's long-term earning potential

The staking numbers also deserve some attention

Only 37 wallets are currently staking, compared to roughly 2,300 reported token holders

The staking system might still be in its early stages, but participation is clearly limited for now

5. How does Darkwoods compare to Venice AI?

Darkwoods shares some similarities with Venice AI, especially when it comes to privacy-focused AI and connecting product revenue to token value

However, I don't think these two projects are anywhere near the same stage

Venice already has a much more established brand, a larger ecosystem, and a significantly bigger user base

Darkwoods, on the other hand, is still very early and needs to prove that it can attract and retain users

Where Darkwoods might have an opportunity is in its development speed, competitive pricing, and creative workflows like Director Mode

But to build a real long-term competitive advantage, they'll eventually need more than just integrations with existing AI models

Because realistically, other platforms can build similar integrations too

What I'd like to see is Darkwoods gradually developing more proprietary technology, improving the overall product experience, and most importantly, building a real user community rather than just a community of token holders

6. Catalysts I'm watching

There are a few things on the Darkwoods roadmap that I think are worth keeping an eye on

First is Prompt to Earn

This is a planned program that would reward users with points or other incentives for interacting with the platform's AI products

If executed properly, it could help attract new users and encourage them to try the product

However, I'm always a little cautious with these kinds of programs. People farming rewards aren't necessarily the same people who will continue paying for the product afterward

Next is DarkRoom Cinema and their proprietary AI models

The team has already introduced DarkRoom Cinema 1.0, and further development of their own models could gradually reduce their dependence on third-party providers

The biggest long-term catalyst is probably the Darkwoods Inference Network

Their goal is to eventually operate their own AI inference infrastructure rather than remain just another platform aggregating existing models

It's an ambitious direction, but it would also require significant resources and time

For now, there's no sufficiently clear timeline for me to treat this as a near-term catalyst

Other planned developments include expanded payment options, a mobile app, and continued improvements to Director Mode

Overall, the team has quite a few things in the pipeline

But I haven't seen a confirmed major catalyst yet, such as a strategic partnership or major listing that could immediately bring the project to a much larger audience

7. Risks I wouldn't ignore

Despite the positives, $DARK is still a high-risk speculative play

The first issue is that the team is completely anonymous

I don't have anything against anonymous teams. Crypto has plenty of successful projects built by anonymous developers

But when you're building AI infrastructure and handling user data, being able to verify the team's technical capabilities and security practices becomes much more important

Second, I haven't seen a credible independent audit fully validating the platform's privacy and security claims

Having verified smart contract source code on an explorer is not the same thing as having an independent security audit

Third is liquidity

Based on the data I've collected, liquidity has generally been around $100K–$180K

With liquidity that thin, a token sitting at a $3M–$6M market cap can still experience significant price swings from relatively modest buying or selling pressure

That's also why I don't want to judge $DARK purely based on a few strong green candles

And finally, while the token reportedly has around 2,300 holders, attention from major KOLs is still fairly limited

A few accounts, including @cryptolyxe, have mentioned the project, but I haven't seen enough widespread attention to consider $DARK one of the leading AI narratives in the market

That could become an opportunity if the project continues growing, but it's also a risk if fresh liquidity never arrives

8. Chart analysis and my trading plan

Looking at the 1H chart, $DARK has already experienced several strong rallies, with market cap reaching around $6M on multiple occasions before seeing sharp pullbacks

At the time I checked the chart, market cap was sitting around $3.63M, following a recent move toward the $6M–$6.5M area

This tells me the token can still attract speculative liquidity, but there's also considerable selling pressure at higher valuations

Personally, I'm not interested in FOMOing after moves like that

The area I'm watching is around $2.5M–$3.5M market cap, especially if price starts consolidating there and selling volume gradually fades

If it loses $2M, I'll reassess the entire price structure and thesis rather than blindly averaging down

On the upside, if $DARK reclaims the $4M–$5M area with healthy volume and maintains a stronger market structure, a retest of previous highs becomes more interesting

Of course, these are just areas I'm watching on the chart, not guaranteed entry signals

I'd still like to examine the holder distribution, major wallets, and on-chain activity

Notebooklm 幻灯片中文字体修复升级版：升级 4K满足大屏投影需求+修正画面瑕疵+去水印

前两天分享了一个用 Gemini 修复 Notebooklm 幻灯片中文笔画崩坏的方法，很受大家欢迎。其实升级到 2K 字体细节仍不够完美，个别复杂的字还是会有笔画模糊的情况。今天再分享一个进阶点的方法：使用谷歌 AI studio 指定 4K 输出，笔画细节几乎可以达到真实文字输入的效果了，即使投影到大屏幕也能完美显示。另外还可以通过提示词修复画面中的瑕疵（比如文字可读性差，图标错误，配图不恰当等），AI studio 里可以生成不带水印的图片，再用提示词去掉 Notebooklm 自带的水印就能实现字体完美无水印的效果了。

比如图中的例子：画面右侧背景太暗文字可读性很差，通过提示词“请将该图片用最高分辨率重新生成，修复文字错误，去掉水印，并修复画面右侧文字可读性的问题”进行整体修复。大家可以根据具体画面中的瑕疵用针对性的提示词进行修复，如果修复后画面变化过大，可以追加“画面其他部分保持不变”。

AI studio 现在免费额度几乎没有了，想要正常使用需要绑定支付方式才行还是有点门槛的。大家也可以选择支持 Nano banana pro 的第三方服务，比如 Lovart，freepik等或者使用 AI 客户端搭配 API key 的方式。

2108567403642998914.name: 刘老板
2108567403642998914.text:
《迈克尔杰克逊演唱会 AI 视频制作保姆级教程》

首先需要下载原视频。打开 B 站，在迈克尔·杰克逊相关视频里，左下角第一个。你可以按键盘上的 Shift 加 S，画面上会有「选择录制」，然后录屏。这是一种办法。

第二种办法：点击右上角有一个「扩展」，我们搜索扩展。扩展里面搜「B 站视频下载」，选择一个 B 站视频下载插件。添加之后，点击扩展，点击「从工具栏上固定」。好，点击这个图标，我们选择「大视频优先」，第一个，点击下载。这样就可以下载视频了。

点击浏览器，搜「必剪」，找到必剪桌面版，点击立即下载。下载完之后打开必剪，拖入我们刚刚下载好的原视频。选中想要的片段，Ctrl+B 裁切，裁完 Ctrl+C，Ctrl+V 把它复制到上面去。我们先不要去截取人物反应的镜头，后面我们会单独获取人物反应的镜头。

我们这里需要全部截选迈克尔·杰克逊相关的视频镜头。这里是迈克尔·杰克逊跳到舞台上。好，这段先截。中间这一段暂时先不要，后面有相同档号，继续操作。获取所有麦克相关的镜头，把它们全部框选出来，按键盘上的 Ctrl+C，点击画面上方的「新建视频轨道」。好，Ctrl+V 粘贴，然后选择「主轨磁吸」，把它们吸附上来。

这里我全部裁剪完了，给大家看一下。好，就是迈克尔·杰克逊站到上面、好转圈、好跳舞、唱歌，整个视频就这样。然后我们按键盘上的 I 确定入点，按 O 确定出点。注意，每一段视频它要大于 2 秒、小于 15 秒。点击右上角导出，画面上右方可以看到你现在时长是多少。时长 12 秒，这一段可以。确定一段导出来之后，我们再按一次 I，然后再按一次 O。

把剩下的、原视频中最开始的部分，把一些大观众反应的镜头，鼓掌、欢呼，像这样，把它们单独再归一类。操作同上，点击「新建时间线」，把它们单独归一类。来看一下，这是第一个反应镜头，第二个反应镜头，第三个反应镜头。有了这三个反应镜头之后，这几个镜头就导出。

打开浏览器，我们搜索 Liblib 官网，找到 Liblib 官网打开，点击「新建画布」。这里你除了可以用 Liblib，也可以用即梦，也可以用可灵，也可以用 Runway，用哪个也可以，免费的。而且已充值的积分，是进 Liblib 官方的「我的口袋」里面。Liblib 我的口袋里面……还请点开我们上传自己拍的四张图片。因为这张图片像这样，控件就多点一个加号。顾名思义，先分一个模型，点击输入提示词：我想生成四视图。这个英文它会自动帮你写提示词。OK，提交生成。这里就成功生成了人物的四视图。

有了这张四视图之后，我截了一张之前十二分女装的一张图片，同时把这个图片和四视图再拉一个节点出来：参考图二的人物，按照图一的格式排版，制作人物四视图。这里它自动生成提示词，并且制作好了。我们再试做一些观众的图片，这样。这是一个蓝色头发的图片，这个是男娃的图片。

有了人物四视图之后，我们上传刚才导出的原片。把四视图和上传的视频原片，拉一个视频节点，输入这个提示词：把视频里面的人物严格替换成参考图，并保持场景、舞台等。这条提示词是我自己写的，这条提示词肯定不行了，所以就告诉 AI，能让他帮我们优化一下提示词。你可以在 AI 给你提示词之后，选择继续生成；或者是把这个提示词全部复制下来，选择一个视频，拖出一个视频节点，然后在视频节点这里粘贴，把所有的提示词粘贴下来，该 @ 的 @ 出来。

视频模型我们选择 Seedance 2.0 Fast，就可以成功生成。要选择 Seedance 2.0 的话，它的积分会更多一些。比例也是 16:9，画质是 720P，音频选择开启，码率选择高码率。这里我同时让 AI 生成了一版，然后又复制了一版。我们来看一下这些 AI 生成的：前面三个镜头它全都没有替换，到后面这个镜头它替换成功。把跑过的提示词复制生成的来看一眼，也是前面跳出来那些都没有替换成功。
这里就需要我们多去抽卡。这些因为刚开始跳出来那个人物太模糊了，然后不好替换，所以 AI 也没有替换成功。这里我多抽了几次卡，来看一下，这个它就成功了，跳出来人物是有的。那我怎么样才能少抽卡呢？你这里可以直接拿我二创的视频去生成三创视频。因为它原创视频刚跳出来那一段非常模糊，而我的二创视频刚跳出来这里人物是比较清晰的，它也更方便你替换人物一些。
再接下还有一种情况：这里我用片段 3 去生成的时候，它会报错，会有版权问题提示，因为它可以识别到这个是迈克尔·杰克逊本人，用他的这个肖像去生成会报错。这个问题的解决办法，就是你不要用 Seedance 2.0，也不要用 Seedance 2.0 Fast，你换用 MiniMax。

人物跳舞镜头做完之后，我们就要做一些反应镜头。这里是把原本的三个观众的图片，还有这个视频，拖出来一个 AI 的节点：根据参考图 1、参考图 2、参考图 3 依次排顺序，替换参考视频里的三个镜头里面出现的人物观众。再帮我优化一下提示词。这里它就是要先跟我确认，问我具体要替换哪些。视频生成之后呢，把视频先生成出来了。这些 AI 的生成来看一眼：这一版第三个人物没生出来。我们直接选择 AI，在这里跟他说，第三个镜头人物没生成出

2002326764371038373.name: sundyme
2002326764371038373.text:
一个提示词修复Notebooklm幻灯片中文字体崩坏。
Notebooklm 真的是一个神级知识学习工具，生成的幻灯片质量也非常高，但有一个痛点：生成的幻灯片图片是1K（1376*768），中文正文小字细节笔画会崩坏，虽然能认出来但是展示起来非常不美观。经过测试找到一个修复的方式：要将图片下载后在Gemini中用提示词“请将该图片用最高分辨率重新生成，修复文字错误”重新生成，然后点击图片右上角图标下载高清版。这样可以得到2K版，画面几乎看不出差别，中文字体清晰度得到极大改善，崩坏的情况几乎没有了，大家可以放大两张图片看对比。

2108805100236136717.text:
真是挖到宝了！！
感觉可以直接拿来接单变现！

这是我见过最规范的用AI做Logo设计的Skill ！！
一个大神设计师把品牌设计的工作流程、1400多个真实 Logo 参考，以及测试和导出工具，整理成一个 Skill。
看了一下，完全是按照专业设计流程规范来的！

先调研品牌做什么、用户是谁、想传递什么感觉，再研究同行常见的设计。
然后提出 8–12 个创意，从中挑出差异最大的三个，实际画成 SVG。
设计过程中先画黑白稿，确定轮廓和结构后再讨论颜色。
三个方案完成后，还要测试、修改，整理成一张对比图，告诉你推荐哪个、理由是什么。
等你选定方向，再继续制作完整的 Logo 套件。

更有意思的是，这套Skill会完全颠覆常规设计思路！！
比如，咖啡品牌只会画杯子，安全工具只会画盾牌、智能产品只会画大脑......
它会让 Agent 先研究参考库，把品类里用得太多的元素列出来，再探索独特性的表达。

并且完成之后，还会有自检查！
检查SVG 代码还不够，还要渲染成图片检查。
配套的脚本还会自动检查字体依赖、混入的位图、过于复杂的路径、细小到可能消失的结构等问题。
一整套流程下来，确保Logo设计的美观和规范。
最后确认之后，会输出黑白版、单色版、横版和竖版组合、Favicon、App 图标，以及简明使用指南。

作者还开源了 28 个虚构品牌的完整案例，从咖啡店到 SaaS，都能看到概念方案和选定方向的应用效果。
试了一试，确实比几句提示词生成出来的Logo设计图更加高级，关键是放大缩小都不会糊！！

完全可以应对专业场景需求！
开源地址放下面了，有兴趣可以试试！

2095439740128706866.name: Morry.AI
2095439740128706866.text:
建议内容创作者都形成一套「个人视觉IP」。

内容做得再好，如果遮住账号名就没人认出是你，那你的个人 IP 只做了一半。

个人 IP 视觉的作用很直接：
让别人刷到图片的第一眼，就知道这是你的内容。

不会设计也没关系。先找到你喜欢的图片，再反推出它的头像、字体、角色、插画和品牌规则，慢慢搭出自己的视觉体系。

下面这 5 组个人 IP 视觉反推提示词，可以直接拿去用。

⸻

01｜个人头像 / AI Avatar

反推 Prompt：

请反推这张头像的视觉设计 Prompt。

详细拆解人物外貌、五官、发型、表情、服装、头肩比例、人物在画面中的占比、镜头角度、背景设计、品牌色、光线、描边、阴影、材质以及整体风格。

重点分析这张图片为什么适合作为社交媒体头像，以及在小尺寸显示下仍然具有辨识度的设计特征。

⸻

02｜字体 / 文字视觉设计

反推 Prompt：

请详细反推图片中文字的字体视觉效果。

分析字体类型、字重、宽窄比例、笔画、衬线/无衬线、倾斜程度、字距、行距、排列方式，以及描边、渐变、发光、阴影、浮雕、倒角、液态、金属、玻璃、充气等特殊效果。

同时分析文字与背景的关系、配色以及整体设计风格，生成完整的字体视觉设计 Prompt。

⸻

03｜IP / Q版角色

反推 Prompt：

请按照专业 IP 角色设计的方式反推这张图片。

重点分析：角色原型、头身比例、身体结构、五官比例、眼睛、嘴巴、表情、发型、服装、配饰、标志性元素、动作姿态、主辅配色。

如果是实体潮玩，还需分析 PVC、树脂、陶瓷、黏土、毛绒等材质，以及表面粗糙度、反射、灯光、底座和产品展示方式。

最后生成可以用于创造同类 IP 视觉效果的完整 Prompt。

⸻

04｜插画 / 手绘

反推 Prompt：

请从专业插画师角度反推这张图片。

分析绘画媒介、线条、笔触、轮廓、平涂/厚涂、水彩/油画/彩铅/数字绘画、颜色、肌理、人物或场景造型、构图和光影。

重点描述能够决定画面风格的技法，而不是只描述“画了什么”。

最终生成完整插画 Prompt。

⸻

05｜完整品牌视觉 / Visual Identity

反推 Prompt：

不要只反推这张图片本身，请尝试反推出它背后的完整品牌视觉语言。

分析品牌主色、辅助色、字体体系、Logo 使用方式、辅助图形、渐变规律、圆角、线条、图标、摄影风格、插画风格、材质、光影、版式和留白。

总结其中可以被重复使用的设计规则，并输出一套品牌视觉 DNA，最后生成能够持续生成同系列图片的母 Prompt。

⸻

不用一上来就憋一整套品牌 VI。

先选一张你真正喜欢的图，从头像、字体或者配色开始反推。

收藏夹里的审美，只有变成可以重复使用的规则，才算是你的视觉资产。

2092947409227944292.name: meng shao
2092947409227944292.text:
对抗 AI 设计 Slop：来自前 Figma 工程师的七条方法论

1. 始终着眼整体
设计过程本质上是三步循环（源自 Christopher Alexander「形式综合论」）：
  1. 列出所有设计约束；
  2. 构思满足约束的多种方案；
  3. 若发现约束需增删，回到第一步重新整体推演。

关键警告：最常见的错误是跳过第 3 步，陷入"打地鼠式设计"——用户一反馈困惑就立即局部修补。AI 加剧了这种倾向（"把 X 做得更显眼""给 Y 加个入口"式的提示词），最终产出随机取舍、彼此割裂的拼布式界面。

正确做法：收到反馈先判断它是否改变了设计约束，再谈方案。作者团队用一份"小痛点文档"积累次要问题，待重设计时统一、连贯地解决，避免过度反应。

2. 做减法
Agent 天生爱"加东西"——多余文案、分割线、图标，正如它在代码里爱加冗余 try-catch、重复实现工具函数。产出的设计"比工程师手画的好看，但其实挺糟"。对策很简单：逐个元素追问"我真的需要它吗？"

3. 在设计工具里迭代
不要在真实产品代码里迭代设计。"原型引力"是隐形杀手：一旦 Agent 在代码库里搭出第一版，人就会倾向于在其上修修补补，而不再探索其他可能；且代码库上下文会迫使 Agent 生成与现有实现强行嫁接的方案。应使用 Figma（作者眼中仍是最佳，AI 集成日益增强）、Cursor Design Mode、Claude Design 或 HTML 原型等专用工具，并让 AI 为每个方案生成 3–4 个变体。

4. 使用组件与组件库
视图与逻辑分离、构建可复用组件——对工程师显而易见但极其重要，可避免"按钮被反复重实现"的视觉拼布。作者团队的实践：维护一个 /showcase 页面，让 Agent 先在此构建和调试 UI 组件，再接入主应用。

5. 使用预览部署
评估设计的最佳方式是真实数据。即使 Agent 完全按指令实现，拿到真实数据上手后仍可能发现不对——打磨和返工不可避免。对涉及前后端的大功能，作者团队将前后端拆成独立 PR：后端靠单元/集成测试验证，前端靠预览部署链接供人工验证。

6. 学会"偷"
绝大多数 UX 问题早已被人解决，正确的做法是取各家之长重新组合。优秀设计师开案第一件事都是收集大量竞品截图——工程师也应如此，这些截图还是喂给 Agent 的绝佳上下文。

7. 磨练品味
品味即对自身体验的反思能力，是创造而非制造 slop 的必要条件。产品工程师擅长识别"设计不对"，却缺乏修复它的"方案库"——这只能靠反复尝试与反思来积累。过程有趣但也残酷：在"够好"之前要承受密集的批评。作者团队没有全职设计师，采用"打谷式"方法：把设计扔到中间，团队一起"拿棍子敲打"直到满意。

AI 能加速设计的执行，但设计的判断力仍在人：用约束驱动整体思考、对 AI 的"加法冲动"做减法、在专用工具中探索多方案、以组件化和预览部署保证质量、借鉴成熟方案，并以持续反思培养品味——这才是工程师借助 AI 产出好设计的完整闭环。

2091397538628706777.name: Derek Wen｜德里克文
2091397538628706777.text:
【AI绘画每日一词】物字共生 🔤🛠️

很多所谓的AI标志设计，只是左边放一个图标，右边写一行文字。

图和字互不相干，更像插图加标题。

“物字共生”要做的，是把器物的结构拆进文字笔画里：字仍然能读，物也一眼能认，两者共同形成一个新的视觉符号。

🎯 核心提示词

为准确文字【2—4个中文字符／简短英文单词】设计一枚“物字共生”标志，结合器物【物品／工具／乐器／食物／动物】。

首先分析器物最有辨识度的结构：主体轮廓、把手、开口、关节、按钮、底座、尖端、纹理或运动轨迹。

再将这些结构映射到文字笔画中：器物的主体承担主笔画，把手或开口融入字形留白，关节成为转折点，功能性部件成为点、撇、捺或装饰细节。

文字内容、顺序和字数必须完全准确。不要把器物简单放在文字旁边，也不要用插图遮挡文字。最终标志应同时满足：

① 缩小后文字仍然清楚可读
② 去掉颜色后器物轮廓仍能识别
③ 字与物形成一个不可拆分的整体
单一完整标志，居中构图，纯色背景，黑白矢量设计，边缘干净，笔画粗细统一，保留必要负空间。不要海报场景、立体模型、样机、阴影、渐变、复杂纹理和多余文字。
💡 核心逻辑

这类提示词的关键不是“把什么东西塞进字里”，而是找到二者共用的结构。

例如，镜头可以对应圆形字腔，琴弦可以变成竖向笔画，车架可以承担斜线结构，蒸汽可以延伸为书法收笔。

真正好的融合，不靠解释就能被看懂。

🔁 延伸玩法

• 电影片名＋剧情核心道具
• 餐饮品牌＋代表食材或厨具
• 音乐栏目＋乐器和声波结构
• 运动品牌＋球具、跑道或动作轨迹
• 非遗项目＋传统工具和制作纹样
• 个人IP名称＋角色标志性配件

⚙️ 参数技巧

先生成纯黑白版本，通过“缩略图测试”后再增加材质和颜色。文字最好控制在2—4个汉字，字越多，融合后越容易失去可读性。
如果用于正式商标，应人工核对文字、调整矢量节点并进行商标检索；AI生成结果更适合作为创意草案，不宜未经修改直接注册。
📌 一句话总结
普通标志让图形陪着文字，物字共生让图形真正长进文字里。

2052739735043662333.name: 小鹏Digital
2052739735043662333.text:
Telegram老板强制发消息了，10项重要更新：

1.在任何聊天里直接 @ 访客 AI 机器人
在私聊或群聊中输入 @机器人用户名，就能让 AI 在当前对话里回答、查资料、生成文本或图片等。

机器人只能看到被提及的那条消息及其回复，不能读取整个聊天记录，隐私控制更细。

2.机器人之间可以互相对话（Bot-to-Bot）
机器人现在不仅能回复人类用户，也可以回复其他机器人。

这样可以组合多个 AI 或自动化机器人，实现更复杂的自动工作流和“自治代理”。

3.机器人支持流式输出文本
机器人回复可以像 ChatGPT 一样边生成边展示，而不是等整段生成完再发出来。

新的 Bot API 让这种流式输出更高效，并配有新的显示动画，体验更顺滑。

4.个人资料里的聊天自动化
每个用户都可以把一个机器人连接到自己的个人资料，让它代你回复消息。

你可以配置哪些聊天允许机器人接管，比如排除所有联系人、仅处理新私聊等。

5.自定义 AI 文本风格（AI Styles）
在 AI 文本编辑器里，你可以用自己的提示词打造独特写作风格，用于帖子、推广文案等统一语气。

每个自定义风格都有可分享链接，别人可以预览示例效果并一键添加到自己的编辑器中。

6.1亿+ 表情与贴纸的 AI 搜索
现在可以在贴纸面板里搜索超过 1 亿个用户创作的表情和贴纸。

搜索支持 36 种语言关键词，由运行在 Cocoon Network 上的自研 AI 模型为海量贴纸打标签并匹配。

7.民意调查的统计图表
群组和频道中的投票，现在管理员可以看到每个选项随时间变化的互动图表。

投票数达到 100 票后会出现这些统计图，方便分析趋势和参与度。

8.投票的自定义参与限制
频道管理员可以限制谁可以参加投票，例如仅限订阅者，或限定来自特定国家/地区的用户。

这些限制可以在投票设置中启用“仅限订阅者”或“按国家/地区限制”。

9.静默定时消息
安排定时发送消息时，支持设为静音发送，不会打扰收件人的通知。

操作方式是长按发送按钮，选择“预定消息”，然后点击铃铛图标关闭提示音。

10.管理员可以批量移除表情反应
群管理员可以删除某个用户在消息上的表情反应。

也可以双击快速删除该用户在该消息上的所有表情反应，方便维护秩序。

另外，Telegram 本次还顺带做了 200 多项跨平台改进和 Bug 修复，不过上面这 10 条就是最核心、最“有感”的新能力
#telegram

2047907878477111764.name: 徐跑跑
2047907878477111764.text:
爆款 GPT Image 2.0 案例&提示词合集来啦！

这次不要只拿它生成头像了，真正强的是：
海报、信息图、漫画分镜、产品广告、社媒封面、项目路线图，全都能直接出成品感。

我整理了 6 个最适合创作者/运营/项目方直接复制的场景：

1️⃣ 爆款海报
为「AI Agent 工具发布」设计一张现代科技感海报，竖版 4:5，主标题清晰醒目，副标题解释产品价值，使用黑白灰+荧光绿点缀，包含抽象网络、代码窗口、智能体节点，整体像高端 SaaS 发布海报，文字必须准确可读。

2️⃣ X 长图封面
生成一张适合 X/Twitter 长文的封面图，主题是「2026 AI 工具趋势」，横版 16:9，风格干净高级，包含标题、3个关键词：Agent / Workflow / Automation，背景是桌面工作流、浏览器、终端、数据面板的组合，排版像科技媒体头图。

3️⃣ 产品广告图
为一款 Web3 钱包安全工具生成广告图，画面中心是一部手机展示钱包界面，周围有链上地址、风险预警、盾牌图标、交易路径可视化，风格专业可信，中文标题：让每一笔链上操作更安全。

4️⃣ 信息图
制作一张中文信息图，主题是「AI Agent 的 5 层能力」，包含：理解任务、调用工具、读取数据、执行操作、复盘优化。用清晰层级结构展示，每一层配一个小图标，白底，科技蓝点缀。

5️⃣ 漫画分镜
生成一页 4 格漫画，讲一个创作者从手动找资料、写文案、做图，到用 AI Agent 自动完成工作流的过程。风格轻松幽默，人物一致，中文对白简短清晰，最后一格突出“效率翻倍”。

6️⃣ 项目路线图
为一个 AI x Crypto 项目生成路线图视觉图，包含 Q2、Q3、Q4 三个阶段：MVP、Agent Marketplace、Onchain Automation。风格像融资 Deck 里的产品页，干净、可信、有未来感，文字清晰可读。

这次 GPT Image 2.0 最适合的不是“随便画一张图”。

而是把创作者脑子里的模糊想法，直接变成能发、能卖、能展示的视觉资产。

做内容的人，建议把这 6 类提示词存下来。

以后发推、做封面、写研报、做项目图，都能省很多时间。

2003318596722724917.name: 歸藏(guizang.ai)
2003318596722724917.text:
Open AI 这个年终总结不行，藏师傅给他补一下

🍌 Nano Banana Pro 提示词：

为你的 ChatGPT 年终总结做一张分享图

Open AI 这个年终总结还是没国内大厂专业，分享图该有的信息都没有，我自己用大香蕉搞了一套提示词

把你的总结截图和提示词扔给 Nano Banana 就行

-------提示词------

任务目标：
基于用户同时上传的年终总结截图中的数据和信息，设计一张风格鲜明、极具视觉冲击力的 3D 年终总结海报，用户名 [guizang]

整体风格与情绪（固定风格）：
核心风格： 融合 3D 趋势、游戏化元素和高饱和度色彩。
材质感： 画面主体呈现精致的黏土（Clay）或软塑胶材质渲染，边缘圆润，光影柔和，给人一种“盲盒玩具”的亲切感。

排版感： 整体布局要像一份精致的高级杂志，疏密有致，信息架构清晰。文字排版简洁明了，不要添加任何卡片、胶囊或底框类的装饰背景。

画面主体（核心视觉）：
视觉中心是一颗巨大的、紧密堆叠的 Q 版 3D 黏土球体。球体的组成元素需要根据用户上传截图中的具体内容来动态生成：

数据气泡： 将截图中提取的关键数字和对应的标签（例如：消息总数、聊天次数、生成图片数、活跃度排名等）制作成圆润的黏土数据气泡嵌入球体。

主题图标： 根据截图体现的用户兴趣点，添加相应的通用黏土图标（例如：游戏手柄、大脑、图表、对话气泡等）。

类别建筑（核心要求）： 分析截图中的内容侧重点，在球体中融入几座代表不同聊天品类的精致微缩黏土建筑。例如：
如果包含 AI/技术内容，加入一座带有科技感的未来数据中心建筑。
如果包含游戏内容，加入一座像素风格的游戏城堡。
如果包含创意/艺术内容，加入一个微型艺术工作室。
组合方式： 所有这些元素（气泡、图标、建筑）必须非常紧密、融洽地挤在一起，无缝组成一个完美的球形，不露出内部结构。

背景设计（固定框架）：
底色： 采用高饱和度的暖橙色到柔和紫色的渐变背景（参考之前的风格）。

背景文字： 在星球背后，放置六个巨大的、带有喷溅纹理和反向蚀刻效果的汉字，主题可以是“冒险 创新 探索”（上排）和“创造 硬核 冲击”（下排），部分被球体遮挡，增加街头硬核感。

信息架构与排版（内容从截图中提取）：
顶部 (Header)： 放置白色的 ChatGPT Logo，并根据截图信息生成标题，格式为：“[从截图中提取的用户名] 的 [年份] 年终总结”。

底部数据区 (Data Grid)： 在球体下方，创建一个极简的 2x2 纯文字数据网格。从截图中选取 4 个最核心的数据，使用超粗无衬线字体展示大数字，并配上相应的文字标签和有趣的社交属性短语（例如：“社交牛逼症”、“话痨”、“六边形战士”等，依据数据特性生成）。
页脚总结 (Footer)： 在最底部用小字排版两段文字，内容直接从用户截图中的总结段落（如“你的聊天风格”和“年度亮点”）提取。

2094667051231269039.name: Morry.AI
2094667051231269039.text:
内容创作者必须要收藏的 6 组「图片反推提示词」

真正有用的图片反推，不是复述图上有什么。

而是拆出它为什么能让人停下来、为什么看起来高级，以及怎么复刻这套设计逻辑。

01｜X / 小红书 / 公众号封面

反推 Prompt：

请反推这张社交媒体封面的设计。

分析图片比例、主题、视觉 Hook、主体位置、标题区域、文字大小关系、背景、品牌色、图形、人物、Logo、留白以及信息层级。

重点分析为什么这张图能够在信息流缩略图状态下吸引注意力。

最后生成一份同风格封面 Prompt，并明确标注主体区、标题区和安全留白区。

⸻

02｜信息图 / Infographic

反推 Prompt：

请从信息设计师角度反推这张信息图。

不要只描述内容，重点分析它如何组织信息。

拆解标题、模块、卡片、编号、图标、连接线、数据、注释、分割线、网格系统、阅读顺序、对齐方式、留白、字体层级、颜色层级以及重点信息强调方式。

总结其版式规则，并生成能够制作同类型信息图的完整 Prompt。

⸻

03｜数据可视化 / Dashboard

反推 Prompt：

请反推这张数据可视化图片的设计系统。

分析 Dashboard 布局、卡片数量、网格、数据指标、折线图、柱状图、饼图、标签、图例、数字字号、字体、颜色、背景、圆角、阴影、边框和交互感。

判断属于金融终端、SaaS Dashboard、AI Dashboard、Web3 数据面板还是其他类型，并生成完整设计 Prompt。

⸻

04｜YouTube Thumbnail / 视频封面

反推 Prompt：

请按照高点击率 YouTube Thumbnail 的设计逻辑反推这张图片。

分析人物表情、主体大小、视觉冲突、前后景、文字数量、字体大小、描边、颜色对比、箭头/图标/辅助元素以及背景虚化方式。

重点分析缩小后仍然能够被识别的元素，以及制造好奇心的视觉设计方式。

生成完整 Thumbnail Prompt。

⸻

05｜Meme / 梗图

反推 Prompt：

请分析并反推这张 Meme 图片。

首先识别原图结构以及梗的核心逻辑，分析人物、动作、表情、场景、文字位置和视觉反差。

重点说明它为什么好笑，以及幽默来自人物替换、文字反差、场景错位、夸张还是网络文化引用。

最后生成可以保持原梗结构但替换主题内容的 AI 图片 Prompt。

⸻

06｜插画 / 手绘

反推 Prompt：

请从专业插画师角度反推这张图片。

分析绘画媒介、线条、笔触、轮廓、平涂/厚涂、水彩/油画/彩铅/数字绘画、颜色、肌理、人物或场景造型、构图和光影。

重点描述能够决定画面风格的技法，而不是只描述“画了什么”。

最终生成完整插画 Prompt。

⸻

这 6 组提示词都是内容创作者的常用场景。

先收藏，下次刷到好图就直接复制来用。

2094073021573259281.name: meng shao
2094073021573259281.text:
Grok Bot Templates 分享功能发布！

Templates 怎么发、怎么用、会包含哪些信息、会泄露隐私吗？ @mattyp 发布的 7 分钟视频，给我们都讲明白了！

Templates 101
 点「Share as template」只是让 Bot 给自己打包装箱，不会立刻公开。Bot 自己决定带什么、丢掉什么：保留对别人有用的 memories / plugins / skills / routines，丢掉个人或内部记忆。自定义 MCP、脚本、私有代码、密钥都不进模板。官方插件（演示里是 Pstack、GitHub，以及和 Cursor 的耦合）会带上。

Sharing
 入口在 Bot 设置右下角。生成的是一份未发布、已脱敏的草稿。可点 View details，逐项看 context、memories、integrations。

Publishing
 发布范围只有两档：公开，或 仅团队。他的 Loop Bot 绑的是 SpaceX 内部写代码流程，他说如果要内部分享，会选 team only。发布后拿到一条链接，打开就是模板页。

Installing
 对方点 Add to Grok Bot → 先审阅 context 和 integrations → 再确认 Add to Bot。安装出来的是一只全新 Bot，不是合并进你已有的那只；图标、身份都会不同。Bot 会按菜谱自己「安装自己」。官方插件要在新账号侧重装/确认；非官方依赖（MCP、脚本）必须接收方自己补。

复杂模板与写作建议
依赖 API key、MCP、高度定制流程时，模板装完通常还要 setup。他的做法是回去问原 Bot：
把安装和配置说明写进模板，想清楚对方要复现这套流程还缺什么。
Bot 会回头改模板。简单模板不必这么做，官方 share/copy 流程就够。

Evaluating
结尾很实用：把模板当别人写的软件来审，不要当提示词来点。装之前读 details、读 integrations，确认每项都是你预期的。第三方模板可以代表你行动。

Templates 里包含什么、不包含什么？
包含：
· skills、被选中的 memories、官方 plugins
· 官方 connectors（需接收方再确认）
· routines（会带上，但默认暂停且标成 untrusted）
不包含：
· 密钥、私有记忆、自定义 MCP / 脚本 / 代码
· 会话历史、原 Bot 的电脑、已登录会话
· 与你已有 Bot 的合并

2091834138131370179.name: meng shao
2091834138131370179.text:
前端 UI 设计怎么避免"AI 味" ？

@addyosmani 在他 89.4K 🌟 Agent Skills 项目的「Frontend UI Engineering」部分，展开论述了其中很典型的八个模式，看看是不是深有同感，AI 味扑鼻而来。

1. Purple/indigo everything（满屏蓝紫色）
现象：主色默认落在 purple-500/indigo-600 一带，这是 AI 生成界面最著名的一个特征。
模型为何偏爱：Tailwind 官方示例、shadcn/ui 演示主题、Bootstrap 5 的品牌紫、无数教程——紫色在语料中与"现代科技感"强绑定。
问题本质：品牌色是产品最有价值的差异化资产之一。当所有 AI 应用都是紫色时，用户第一眼就能识别出"这是模板/AI 生成的"，信任感瞬间折损。更关键的是，它无视了项目已有的品牌 token。
替代方案的实质：颜色决策权交还给项目。没有品牌色时，也应该先做一次有意的选择，而不是接受模型的统计默认值。

2. Excessive gradients（滥用渐变）
现象：hero 背景渐变、按钮渐变、甚至 bg-clip-text 渐变文字。
模型为何偏爱：2018–2022 年间 Stripe 式渐变落地页在语料中大量存在，模型把"令人印象深刻"与"渐变"关联了起来。
问题本质：成熟的设计系统绝大多数是扁平的，渐变会与系统冲突、制造视觉噪音；渐变文字还会损害对比度和可读性；大面积渐变在低端屏幕上容易出现色带。
注意：这一条反对的不是渐变本身，而是"无设计依据的渐变"。设计系统明确规定的微妙渐变是允许的。

3. Rounded everything（万物大圆角）
现象：卡片、按钮、输入框、图片一律 rounded-2xl。
模型为何偏爱：圆角传递"友好"，是模型眼中不会出错的选项；Tailwind 让一行类名就能实现。
问题本质：这一条的理由最耐人寻味——真实设计中圆角半径是有层级的：小元素（标签、按钮）用小圆角，大容器（卡片、对话框）用大圆角。全部拉满等于放弃了这层视觉语言。而且圆角还是品牌声音的一部分：金融产品的利落直角和消费产品的圆润亲和，传达的是不同的气质。
替代方案的实质：用设计系统的 radius 刻度，按元素尺寸和类型分级使用。

4. Generic hero sections（模板化首屏）
现象：居中大标题 + 副标题 + 两个 CTA 按钮 + 渐变背景——千篇一律的 SaaS 落地页模板。
模型为何偏爱：落地页模板是语料中"网页"这一概念的众数样本。
问题本质：它是模板驱动而非内容驱动——布局不回应产品是什么、用户来做什么。每个产品得到相同的第一印象，等于没有第一印象。
替代方案的实质：Content-first——从真实内容和用户任务出发，让布局为内容服务。

5. Lorem ipsum-style copy（占位文本）
现象："Lorem ipsum""Welcome to our platform""Feature 1/2/3"这类填充文案。
问题本质：这是八条中最技术性、也最容易被低估的一条。占位文本的危害不只是"不专业"，是它会掩盖布局缺陷：Lorem ipsum 长度均匀、行为良好，而真实内容有超长单词、不规则换行、溢出。用假文本调试出来的布局，遇到真实数据才会崩。换句话说，占位文本让测试失去了效力。
替代方案的实质：写"形状接近真实数据"的占位内容——真实长度的任务名、真实格式的日期和金额，让布局在开发阶段就承受真实内容的压力。

6. Oversized padding everywhere（到处超大内边距）
现象：每个容器都是 p-8、p-12，均匀而慷慨。
模型为何偏爱：留白在截图中等于"干净高级"，且统一数值生成起来最容易。
问题本质：视觉层级依赖间距的对比——相关的元素靠近，无关的疏远。处处等距意味着没有分组、没有层级；同时浪费屏幕空间，在移动端和信息密集的仪表盘上代价尤其大。
替代方案的实质：间距应该是设计决策（密度本身就是一种设计语言)，而不是默认值。用刻度，且敢于变化。

7. Stock card grids（千篇一律的卡片网格）
现象：三列等宽卡片网格——特性区、定价区、仪表盘全是它。
模型为何偏爱：这是最容易生成的响应式布局（grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 一行搞定），且在语料中出现频率极高。
问题本质：均匀网格是在声明"所有条目同等重要"——它无视信息优先级和浏览动线。真实产品总有主次之分：主内容应该占据更大的视觉权重，次要内容退后。
替代方案的实质：Purpose-driven layout——布局是信息层级的视觉表达，而不是内容的均分容器。

8. Shadow-heavy design（阴影堆砌）
现象：卡片、按钮、导航栏层层叠 shadow-lg、shadow-xl。
模型为何偏爱：阴影在截图中制造"精致感"，Material Design 风格的示例在语料中占比高。
问题本质：有两层——视觉层面，阴影与内容争夺注意力，且海拔本身是层级信号，万物皆高等于没有高；工程层面，大面积模糊阴影的重绘会拖慢低端设备的滚动性能。这一条是八条中唯一同时指出性能代价的。
替代方案的实质：默认无阴影或极淡阴影，用边框和背景色区分层次；只在设计系统明确规定时使用。

2084105609629364720.name: Derek Wen｜德里克文
2084105609629364720.text:
作品集只晒最终效果？太普通了。
真正让人停下来多看一眼的，是把「改了什么、为什么改、改完更好在哪」全部摊开在一张图上。

🎯 核心提示词（直接复制用）
为【产品改版/人物造型升级/空间设计优化】制作一张3:4竖版“审校痕迹可视化”编辑海报，Visible Design Review。
暖冷灰白背景+严格12列网格。画面中央放占比约65%的完整主视觉（产品界面/人物/建筑/海报），单一画布，不做左右拼图。
在主视觉上精确叠加3处审校标记：半透明旧版轮廓、细线定位框、局部放大圆窗、修改箭头+极短批注。旧版用10%透明度灰红色虚线，新版保持清晰；通过项低饱和绿点，待改项克制琥珀色。
右上角放修改结论（如“层级优化”“信息减负”），左下角3条微型变更记录：【问题】→【调整】→【结果】。不要长段说明。
标题高对比衬线，批注中性无衬线，坐标/尺寸/版本号等宽。信息层级只留三级。
主体材质真实：玻璃屏幕、皮肤纹理、混凝土/金属细节。配色限定象牙白、石墨黑、灰红、低饱和绿+少量琥珀。
整体像设计总监审稿台+建筑校样+高端案例研究。禁止红笔乱画、密集箭头、满屏便利贴、均匀对比图。

💡 核心逻辑
旧版轮廓 → 改了什么
定位框 → 问题在哪
短批注 → 为什么改
新版主体 → 调整后的结果
颜色只表状态，不装饰
普通作品集只给答案；审校痕迹展示判断力。
🔁 延伸：AI生图初稿精修、角色设计逐项校正、游戏UI叠影、商业海报把甲方意见变成视觉证据。
⚙️ 关键控制：审校点3-4处，主体≥60%，旧版叠影8%-15%，每条批注≤8字，红黄绿只表状态。中文多时先无字校样再排版。
📌 一句话
真正专业的视觉，不只让人看到你做得更好，还让人看到你是如何判断“什么才算更好”。
#AI绘画 #提示词 #AIGC #设计审核 #VisibleDesignReview

2114175667734470997.name: 洛克船长
2114175667734470997.text:
这周 GitHub 涨得最猛的十个 AI 开源项目，这周 GitHub 被 AI agent 占领了.

插件、技能、编排、记忆……大家已经不只是在做"更聪明的模型"了，而是在给 agent 造手、造脑子、造记性。一个接一个看下来，真的有点头皮发麻。

下面这十个，每个都值得你停下来看一眼。

01 REA：连续两周第一，疯了

⭐ 375,014｜本周 +88,243
上周它就是第一，结果这周它又涨了将近九万颗星，接着霸榜。
它做的事说起来很简单：你看到别人的 App 有个功能做得好，跟 AI 说一句"帮我搞清楚它是怎么做的"，AI 就会调用 Ghidra、IDA 这些逆向工具，从界面一路拆到二进制，每个结论都附上证据。
更离谱的是，连 Ghidra 本身这周都被带上了趋势榜。
🔗 https://t.co/n9B6flcGRM

02 claude-plugins-official：Anthropic 亲自下场做插件目录

⭐ 44,217｜本周 +4,250
Anthropic 官方管理的 Claude Code 插件目录，已经收了 315 个插件。
一个插件就是一个文件夹：斜杠命令、子 agent、技能、MCP 服务，全装在里面。装一个，Claude Code 一下子就多了一整套本事。GitHub、Figma、Notion、Stripe、Supabase、Vercel 都已经在里面了。
一句 /plugin install 就装好。官方自己也在 README 第一句提醒你：装之前，先确认你信得过它。
🔗 https://t.co/QY2uY6HcTa

03 Ruflo：给 Claude Code 塞进一整个 agent 蜂群

⭐ 78,865｜本周 +3,349
前身叫 Claude Flow。一句 npx ruflo init，Claude Code 就多了 98 个分工明确的 agent：有的规划，有的写代码，有的测试。
路由器把每个任务派给最合适的 agent，做成功的套路存进记忆，下次派得更准。控制台里，每个 agent 在干什么、烧了多少 token、花了多少钱，一清二楚。
一个人带一支 AI 施工队，说的就是这个。
🔗 https://t.co/zx2lQXPOah

04 android/skills：Google 安卓团队亲手写的 agent 技能

⭐ 9,503｜本周 +1,471
Google 安卓官方出的 33 个 Agent Skills。最让我服气的是他们挑技能的思路：专挑大模型做得差的地方下手。模型已经会的，他们一个都不写。
迁移 Compose、排查卡死、分析混淆、车机、手表、XR 眼镜都有。你只要说一句"把我的 App 改成全面屏"，agent 自己就会翻到对应的那本说明书。
🔗 https://t.co/k1k8D51K6S

05 OpenCode：开源版的 Claude Code，而且不绑模型

⭐ 220,865｜本周 +6,765
官方说每个月有 1600 万开发者在用。
它最狠的地方是不绑定任何一家：75 家以上的模型服务商随便接，Claude、GPT、Gemini、本地模型都行，还能直接用你的 Copilot 或 ChatGPT 会员登录。按 Tab 在 build 和 plan 两个 agent 之间切换：一个放开手脚干活，一个只读、先摸清代码再说。
🔗 https://t.co/H3aowTZuCM

06 Orca：一个提示词，五个 agent 同时开工

⭐ 104,266｜本周 +9,545
三月才建库，现在已经十万星，这周涨幅前十里排第二。
同一个需求同时丢给五个 agent，每个都在自己的 git worktree 里干，互不打扰。干完摆在一起比，挑最好的合进去。Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode，三十多种命令行 agent 都能接。
在浏览器里点一下页面元素，它的 HTML、CSS 和截图就直接塞进提示词。agent 干完了，手机上弹通知，躺着就能接着下指令。
🔗 https://t.co/ZeEgfqHzuo

07 cursor/plugins：Cursor 也出插件规范了

⭐ 13,839｜本周 +1,946
121 个官方插件，思路和 Claude Code 一样：一个文件夹，加一份清单。
orchestrate 把大任务拆给一批并行的云端 agent，规划、干活、验证各司其职；advisor 会在做大决定之前，先去请教一个更强的模型。
Claude Code、Cursor、安卓官方，三家的插件仓库同一周一起往上涨。插件和技能，正在变成所有 AI 编程工具的通用语言。
🔗 https://t.co/fvzbExRcR0

08 ai-memory：换工具、换电脑，agent 还记得你

⭐ 13,132｜本周 +3,449
这个解决的是我自己天天遇到的痛点。
Claude Code 做到一半退出，打开 Codex，它会拿到一张交接单：做到哪了、哪些路试过走不通、还剩什么没解决。20 多种 agent 共用一份记忆，全部存成 Markdown 放进 git，你可以直接用 Obsidian 打开、手改。
记忆还会老化：不用的慢慢淡出，常用的留得更久。真的很像人。
🔗 https://t.co/QDVLWudnmr

09 CLI-Anything：让任何软件都能被 agent 直接用

⭐ 56,703｜本周 +3,303
港大数据智能实验室出品。agent 最擅长用命令行，可大多数软件是给人用鼠标点的。
它的办法是给软件套一层命令行外壳。在 Claude Code 里打一句 /cli-anything，后面跟上 GIMP 的源码目录，它就自己跑完七步：分析、设计、实现、测试、写文档、打包。Blender、LibreOffice、FreeCAD 都有了，连《杀戮尖塔 2》都有。
🔗 https://t.co/0BoVWqje1Z

10 ComfyUI：老将不死

⭐ 142,455｜本周 +4,531
前十里唯一一个不是给写代码的人用的，2023 年的老项目，这周照样涨了四千五。
AI 生成被拆成一个个节点，用线连起来就是一条工作流。图片、视频、音频、3D 都能做，新出的开源模型基本第一时间支持。官方说，最大的开源模型，4G 显存加 8G 内存也能跑。
而且它有本地 API，agent 也能直接调它出图。你看，连它都绕回 agent 了。
🔗 https://t.co/hxBSewixYG

再提一个：VoiceStudio，涨得比第 2 到第 10 名都猛
⭐ 83,901｜本周 +12,526
第 11 名，但这周的涨幅其实比第二到第十名都高。
它是完全在本地跑的开源 ElevenLabs 替代品：声音克隆、视频配音、转录、有声书，646 种语言。做内容的朋友，真的值得去看看。
🔗 https://t.co/mcCjppIVAd

AI 越来越疯狂，GitHub 的开源库也就越来越好看。
每个星期我都会把趋势榜过一遍，完整视频版每个项目都配了一台机械动画，演示它是怎么工作的。
下周见。
星数截至 2026 年 10 月 24 日，本周增量来自 GitHub Trending 周榜。

2074819710492061788.name: 老杨啊 | AI产品商业化
2074819710492061788.text:
让 AI 做网页设计，出来的十有八九都一个样：居中大标题、三张一模一样的卡片、紫蓝渐变、emoji、"赋能你的工作流"——这叫 AI 味，SDesign 专门治这个。

一句话：64 套不同调性的网页设计提示词，复制粘给任意 AI，出来的页面有设计师品位，不飘、不烂、不撞款，零安装。

为什么 AI 做的设计总是一个味：

AI 默认往"安全、中庸、讨好所有人"的方向靠，没有人给它具体的审美约束，所有人的输出自然就趋同了。SDesign 做的事情就是把这个约束提前写好塞进去：

（1）6 大美学家族，64 套真不一样的设计——极简留白（Airbnb / Stripe / Notion）、科技暗黑（Linear / Supabase / Warp）、暖色人文（Claude / Cursor / Arc）、电影暗调（Raycast / SpaceX / Runway）、数据密集（Binance / GitHub）、大胆彩色（Duolingo / Canva / Hugging Face）——每一套都是真不一样的调性，不是同一套模板改了个颜色

（2）内置去 AI 味硬规则——不只是说"做得好看一点"，是机械可执行的具体规则：禁止出现居中大标题布局、禁止三卡等分、禁止紫蓝渐变、禁止多余 emoji……Claude 级和更弱的模型实测都能遵守

（3）复制即用，零安装——找到你想要的美学，打开 prompt.md，复制整段，粘给 Claude / ChatGPT / Codex，后面接一句"给我做个 XXX 页面"就行

（4）也能装进 Claude Code 当 SKILL——把这个仓库丢进项目，Claude Code 读 SKILL.md 会自动按你的需求挑美学、套规则，不用每次手动选

（5）手绘插画配图也有——单独一个 illustration/ 模块，给正文文章配一张手绘草图风格的插画，因为精致 AI 配图本身也是 AI 味重灾区

在线直接看 64 套效果：https://t.co/VTZ8z8upyT，点开即用，不用装任何东西。

用 AI 做落地页、产品页、个人网站的兄弟，这套提示词库可以省掉很多来回改稿的时间。

https://t.co/NpBRvlKj40

好东西转给需要的兄弟。🚀

2113554195081257105.name: 不系舟
2113554195081257105.text:
发现一个解决AI生图排版痛点的开源模型。

现在的生图模型越来越强，但一直有个问题没解决：**没办法精准控制排版**。因为排版很难用提示词描述清楚，想调整位置只能反复抽卡。

最近发现模思智能开源的 MOSS-Image，真正解决了这个问题。它支持用 JSON Layout 结构化控图——直接从参数层面指定元素坐标和方位，按预设排版精准生成。

**工作流很简单：**
输入布局 JSON → 导入布局 → 拖动调整位置框 → 保存应用 → 提交生成

我用它做了张咖啡店海报（见图），直接调整 JSON 里的参数，就能改变元素位置、切换排版风格。做广告海报、电商产品图、社媒封面，终于可以把「内容」和「位置」一起精准控制了。

作为纯血国产模型（5B 参数，支持 4K tokens），效果确实超预期。做设计的朋友可以试试。

2097696046260609314.name: 逸尘
2097696046260609314.text:
1.把品牌logo发给GPT Image2.5，让它直出全套周边（我用的Ailu做演示）。

完整提示词：

请以【品牌 Logo 参考图】作为唯一核心视觉输入，为该品牌自动设计并输出一整套完整、统一、可真实生产落地的品牌周边产品系统。

【唯一输入】
Image A = 【品牌 Logo 参考图】

除 Logo 外，不需要用户额外提供品牌名称、配色、风格、IP设定或产品方向。
请你自行从 Logo 中分析并推导完整的品牌视觉语言。

--------------------------------------------------
【第一步：自动解析 Logo】

请先从【品牌 Logo 参考图】中提取并理解：

1. Logo 的核心图形元素
2. Logo 的主体轮廓与识别特征
3. 主色、辅助色、点缀色
4. 图形中具有代表性的局部元素
5. Logo 的线条语言
6. 图形的圆润 / 锐利 / 几何 / 手绘 / 卡通 / 极简属性
7. 品牌可能传递出的情绪与性格
8. Logo 是否包含人物、动物、符号、文字、字母、图腾或抽象图形
9. 哪些视觉元素适合进一步转化成：
   - 图案
   - Icon
   - Badge
   - Pattern
   - 刺绣
   - 印花
   - 压纹
   - 吊牌
   - 包装纹样
   - 装饰元素

不要机械地把 Logo 贴到所有商品上。

核心目标是：
把 Logo 扩展成一套真正完整的「品牌视觉系统」。

--------------------------------------------------
【第二步：建立品牌视觉系统】

基于 Logo 自动建立：

- 主品牌色
- 辅助色
- 中性色
- 高亮色
- 品牌图形语言
- 辅助图形
- 图标系统
- 重复 Pattern
- Logo 局部裁切图案
- 品牌标签
- 小型 Badge
- 刺绣版本
- 单色版本
- 反白版本
- 小尺寸 Logo 版本

所有衍生设计都必须能够让人明显感受到：

“它们属于同一个品牌。”

但是不要让所有产品看起来完全一样。

需要形成：
主 Logo + 次级图形 + 局部元素 + Pattern + 文字排版 + 色彩系统

这样的层级关系。

--------------------------------------------------
【第三步：自动设计完整周边系列】

请至少设计以下 15 类品牌周边：

【服装 Apparel】
1. T-Shirt
2. Hoodie / 卫衣
3. 棒球帽 / 鸭舌帽
4. 袜子

【包袋 Bags】
5. Canvas Tote Bag 帆布袋
6. 小型收纳包 / 化妆包

【办公 Stationery】
7. Notebook 笔记本
8. Pen / Pencil 文具
9. Sticker Sheet 贴纸套装

【数码 Tech】
10. 手机壳
11. Laptop / Tablet Sleeve
12. Desk Mat / Mouse Pad

【生活 Lifestyle】
13. Mug / Coffee Cup
14. Water Bottle / Tumbler
15. Umbrella 或其他适合该品牌的生活用品

【收藏 Collectibles】
16. Acrylic Keychain 亚克力钥匙扣
17. Enamel Pin 珐琅徽章
18. Mascot / Logo Plush Toy 或软质公仔

【品牌包装 Branding】
19. Shopping Bag
20. Packaging Box
21. Hang Tag / 吊牌
22. Thank You Card / 品牌卡片

如果 Logo 本身非常适合开发 IP，可以额外增加：
- 毛绒公仔
- 摆件
- 冰箱贴
- 手机挂件
- 徽章
- Mini Figure
- 盲盒
- 卡套
- 行李牌

如果 Logo 不适合作为角色，则不要强行拟人化。

--------------------------------------------------
【第四步：每件产品必须采用不同的 Logo 应用方式】

不要简单复制粘贴同一个 Logo。

不同产品可以分别采用：

- 完整 Logo
- Logo 局部裁切
- 轮廓
- 单色 Logo
- 刺绣 Logo
- 小尺寸胸标
- Oversized Graphic
- Repeat Pattern
- Icon
- Badge
- Logo Monogram
- 局部纹理
- 边角装饰
- 吊牌
- 内标
- Side Label
- Packaging Pattern

例如：

T-Shirt：
可以采用大型主视觉印花。

Hoodie：
可以采用小胸标 + 背部大型图形。

帽子：
适合刺绣或简化 Logo。

Tote Bag：
适合 Logo + 辅助图案。

手机壳：
可以使用局部放大元素或重复 Pattern。

贴纸：
可以拆解 Logo 中的不同视觉元素。

钥匙扣：
可以直接沿 Logo 轮廓制作异形结构。

毛绒玩具：
如果 Logo 本身是人物 / 动物 / IP，则立体化其核心形象。

--------------------------------------------------
【第五步：设计风格要求】

最终设计必须具有：

- 高完成度
- 商业品牌感
- 潮流感
- 年轻化
- 高辨识度
- 可真实生产
- 统一但不单调
- 有完整品牌系统感

整体视觉请参考：

品牌官方 Merchandise Collection
潮流品牌 Lookbook
品牌 VI 延展设计
高端电商品牌周边
Creative Brand Guideline
Merchandise Styling Board

不要做成廉价礼品定制店效果。

不要只是：
“白色杯子 + Logo”
“白色衣服 + Logo”
“白色袋子 + Logo”

必须有真正的视觉设计。

--------------------------------------------------
【第六步：Logo 忠实度】

【品牌 Logo 参考图】必须保持高度可识别。

禁止：

- 随意改变 Logo 主体结构
- 改变核心角色身份
- 改变关键轮廓
- 把 Logo 变成完全不同的角色
- 擅自改变 Logo 中已有文字
- 添加不存在的品牌名称
- 错拼 Logo 中的文字

如果原 Logo 中包含文字：
尽可能保留原文字内容与拼写。

如果 Logo 中不存在品牌文字：
不要擅自创造新的品牌名称。

可以使用无语义的辅助排版、小型图形标签、编号、系列名，
但不得让这些元素替代原 Logo。

--------------------------------------------------
【第七步：展示方式】

最终生成一张横向 4:3 的高完成度：

「品牌完整周边系列设计提案 / Brand Merchandise Collection Board」

画面应像专业设计公司向品牌方提交的正式提案。

推荐构图：

顶部：
展示放大的原始 Logo 或 Logo 核心元素，
作为整张视觉板的品牌识别中心。

中间主体：

Professional brand merchandise presentation board,

cohesive visual identity,

2015395070950907972.text:
我敢说技术才是第一生产力，不接受任何反驳，
小红书虚拟爆品分享第28波-PS修图插件 ；靠卖自己的PS插件卖出11万单400多万的收入；
你肯定会想，都AI时代了还在用PS，是不是太LOW了？
明确的告诉你，用PS修图的人绝对要多过于用AI修图的人；
知道AI，但会用AI做图的大有人在，会用AI生图的，且做的好看的能有多少？这就是PS的市场和魅力。

首先说下这个品，他有一定的技术门槛，你得会懂PS，至少要到熟练程度，如果会开发就更好啦，如果不会至少现在AI可以干这活，当然你都不会，你也可以去买或者让别人开发给钱就行；

他的内容形式，也很简单，直接操作自己的插件录屏，录完加上音乐或者介绍就可以发布啦，100%原创，加个水印大部同行不会抄了；

这品如果让老杨来仿一下的话我会这样做；
1、低成本先测试一波，找同行1-3爆款插件，然后找类戊开源且没版权的插件包装一下；
2、然后就是1:1模仿爆款笔记，有二个号同时发不同的笔记，看谁先爆，超过50单，就马上自己用AI开发或者找人开发迭代功能插件；
3、反正一点就是只抄爆品功能，除非有遇到刚需的插件，不然绝不装杯搞创意；
4、用AI+场景功能点+SEO的方案批量做笔记；
5、然后就交给努力和玄学了。

1995426595834671261.name: meng shao
1995426595834671261.text:
对手机端/信息流更友好的信息卡提示词，在小红书和公众号也都在更新「AI 启蒙小伙伴」

--- 以下提示词可直接复制 ---

角色：你是「现代社论风·信息卡设计师」：接收中文内容 → 输出单文件 HTML5 杂志风格信息卡。追求高密度、高对比、视觉冲击力，直接交付完整代码。

🎨 核心设计原则

风格定义：Compact Editorial (紧凑社论)。像一张精美的报纸头版或杂志侧边栏。

布局逻辑：严格的网格系统，拒绝无效留白，信息高密度聚合。
色彩策略：背景 #e5e0d8 / #f7f5f0 (沉稳的报纸灰/米色)。
主色 #2c241b (近乎黑的深褐，用于高对比文字)。
强调 #c17c4a (爱马仕橙/暖棕，用于数据和图标)。
装饰 #dcd6ce (分割线颜色)。

📝 字体与排版
HTML
<link href="<https://t.co/fbzx1nrdFw>" rel="stylesheet"> <link href="<https://t.co/V4amQGNDUX>" rel="stylesheet">
超大标题: 'Noto Serif SC', font-weight: 900, line-height: 0.85 (极其紧凑的衬线大标题)。
数据数字: 'Oswald', font-weight: 700 (高窄的无衬线体，现代感强)。

正文: 'Noto Sans SC', text-sm (清晰易读)。

📐 布局结构 (从上到下)

容器: 固定比例接近 1:1 或 1:1.1，宽度限制 max-w-[640px]。圆角 rounded-xl。

Header (报头):左侧：超大主标题 (4.5rem+)，紧贴顶部。
右侧/底部：小号全大写英文副标，底部由一条粗黑线 (border-b-3) 贯穿，分割头部。

Summary (摘要区):浅色背景块 (bg-[#ece8e1])，左侧带有强调色粗边框 (border-l-4)。

Grid Modules (三列/二列布局):卡片式设计，白色背景，细微边框，内容紧凑。
图标 + 小标题 + 极简说明。

Stats Footer (数据底栏):全深色背景 (bg-[#2c241b])，白色文字。
使用 'Oswald' 字体展示巨大数字，配合全大写极小标签。
这是视觉重心的收尾，必须醒目。

🚀 技术细节与纹理
质感: 必须使用 SVG 噪点纹理 (feTurbulence) 叠加，透明度 0.05，营造纸媒质感。
阴影: box-shadow: 0 20px 40px -10px rgba(60,48,32,0.15) (深邃的悬浮感)。
动效: 元素按顺序上浮 (animation-delay: 0.1s 递增)。
❌ 绝对禁止
禁止大面积留白（Padding 不超过 40px）。
禁止正文行距过大（保持紧凑）。
禁止使用亮纯色（如纯红、纯蓝），保持复古暖色调。
禁止没有任何背景色的透明容器。
输出要求:
仅输出完整 HTML 代码。
包含 Tailwind CSS CDN。
确保标题巨大、数据底栏为深色、整体视觉紧凑帅气。

早上好，朋友们！
今天分享一下使用skill creator创建一个claude skill 。

这个skill 是我开发过程中，比较常见的操作，就是网页上需要图片，我需要自己手动去使用nano banana 去生成网页所需要的图，挺耗费时间的。现在有了skill ，这部分工作也可以让claude code 自己去完成了。

Nano Banana 2.1 prompt: visualizing international carnivore diet dishes

2x2 grid, 16:9, do this for 4 delicious carnivore diet dishes internationallly: CLASSIFY(input) → {
  domain:      miniature_diorama × pop_up_book_engineering × culinary_narrative × tilt_shift_macro
  intent:      narrate + delight + miniaturize (farm → fire → feast in a single spread)
  audience:    food editorial, cookbook publishers, miniature collectors, brand campaigns
  platform:    3:2 or 16:9 landscape hero shot, print + social
  complexity:  extreme (three-act narrative across physical book topology, 1:87 HO figures,
                        diegetic gutter thermodynamics, scale-nesting, Scheimpflug optics)
}

CORE DESIGN LAWS (IMMUTABLE):
  ⚠ THE BOOK IS THE WORLD. THE GUTTER IS THE ENGINE. TIME FLOWS LEFT → RIGHT.
  • Act I  (left page)  = ORIGIN: farming biome as terraced pop-up terrain + harvesters.
  • Act II (gutter)     = TRANSFORMATION: cooking machinery straddling the seam;
                          smoke/steam/fire rises vertically — the spread's only Z-vector.
  • Act III (right page)= FEAST: monumental finished dish + chefs garnishing.
  • Scale: figures & machinery 1:87 HO; the finished dish is MONUMENTAL relative to chefs.
  • Optics: tilt-shift macro, warm diegetic light, 8k. ¬flat illustration ¬cold light.

SEMANTIC_VARIABLES (AI infers from {{DISH}}):
  {{DISH}}         → [e.g., Wood-Fired Neapolitan Pizza, Tonkotsu Ramen, Nigiri Sushi]
  {{ORIGIN_BIOME}} → farming terrain of the hero ingredients (terraced, pop-up)
  {{MACHINERY}}    → the cooking tool that straddles the gutter
  {{PHYSICS_FX}}   → smoke | steam | fire — matched to the cooking method
  {{PLATING}}      → the monumental finished dish
  {{HARVESTERS}}   → 1:87 farmers mid-labor · {{CHEFS}} → 1:87 chefs mid-garnish
  {{HERO_INGREDIENT}} → one ingredient traced through all three acts (raw→cooked→plated)

INFERENCE_EXAMPLE ({{DISH}} = "Wood-Fired Neapolitan Pizza"):
  {{ORIGIN_BIOME}} = terraced tomato vines + golden wheat rows on pop-up hills
  {{MACHINERY}}    = domed wood-fire oven astride the gutter, mouth glowing
  {{PHYSICS_FX}}   = smoke column + ember sparks rising from the seam
  {{PLATING}}      = leopard-charred margherita, basil canopy, oil sheen
  {{HERO_INGREDIENT}} = tomato: on vine (I) → bubbling sauce in oven mouth (II) → sauce on crust (III)

2037649149009760368.name: Bruno Bertolini • awesome.codar.me
2037649149009760368.text:
Usei o mesmo processo pra criar essa landing page. Sem designer. Sem template.

O problema de pedir pra IA "cria uma landing page pra mim" é que ela vai criar. E vai ficar genérica. Parece site de dentista feito no Wix em 2019.

O que muda o resultado é o que você faz antes de pedir. Apliquei o framework exatamente assim pra essa LP:

RESEARCH - REFERÊNCIA VISUAL: Antes de escrever uma palavra, defini o clima da página. Paleta de cores (tons pastel, creme, rosa chá, verde menta), referência de estrutura, e o tipo de sensação que a página precisava passar. No caso, era um produto infantil cristão, precisava ser acolhedor, limpo, leve (sendo honesto, essa parte minha esposa que fez e me passou o que ela queria). Eu juntei algumas referências visuais e mandei pro Claude junto com o briefing.

Sem referência visual, a IA chuta. Com referência, ela executa.

PRD - ESTRUTURA E CONTEÚDO: Ainda no Claude, fui definindo seção por seção. Não cheguei com a estrutura pronta, fui conversando. "Precisa de newsletter?" "Mostra todos os livros ou só os lançados?" "A bio da autora foca em credencial ou em história pessoal?"

A IA me questionou em decisões que eu ia tomar no automático. Tipo a foto do about: eu ia colocar uma foto da família inteira. O Claude sugeriu só mãe e filha, porque o público são mães e a identificação é imediata.

Saí dessa etapa com: estrutura completa de seções, textos de cada bloco, paleta com hex codes, tipografia, espaçamento.

EXEC -  PROMPT DETALHADO PRO AURA: Aqui é onde a maioria começa. E por isso o resultado fica genérico.

Primeiro, gerei a imagem de hero no Nano Banana, depois, com tudo definido antes, montei um prompt que descrevia cada seção com: texto final, cor de background, cor de botão, fonte, tamanho, estilo de card. Colei no https://t.co/R41uoS5vyS, que é melhor que o stitch ou qualquer outra tool pra LP,  e saiu a LP inteira de primeira.

QUALITY GATE - REVISÃO: Olhei a página pronta e fui impiedoso. Tudo que não tinha informação real, tirei. Placeholder de qualquer tipo saiu. Se não tá pronto, não mostra. Depois passei no https://t.co/dmHuxcuvGp pra revisar posicionamento e estrutura de conversão, copy...

O ponto é: LP bonita com IA não é sobre a ferramenta. É sobre o que você alimenta ela antes de pedir. Um designer faria melhor? Sem dúvidas, mas eu nunca seria capaz de criar isso sem AI.

Referência visual → Estrutura com a IA → Prompt detalhado → Execução → Revisão.

https://t.co/qyDJli4R9X

🎬 Long Cinematic AI Video Prompt

Prompt 

A warm, intimate continuation of a dark-fantasy medieval story, vertical 9:16 cinematic format, set at night during heavy snowfall. The scene carries full visual continuity with the earlier cave-birth and cottage-bonding story — same woman, same baby dragon character design, same muted cold-vs-warm color grading philosophy, same photorealistic non-cartoonish creature texture work.

**Scene 1 (0–8s):** Interior of a dim, rustic wooden cabin at night. Through a small frosted window in the background, thick snow falls steadily against a deep blue-black night sky, snow visibly piling on the windowsill. A young woman with long, dark, tousled hair wraps a thick woolen hooded blanket around herself and a small baby dragon nestled against her side, both huddled together for warmth. The dragon has pale translucent pink-cream skin, large glossy amber eyes catching the dim light, delicate curled fin-like horns, and soft frilled ridges along its head. The woman shivers slightly, breath visibly fogging in the cold air, and brings her cupped hands up to her mouth, blowing warm breath into them for warmth, her expression tired, cold, and vulnerable. The dragon peers up at her with wide, attentive, almost worried eyes from beneath the shared blanket.

**Scene 2 (8–14s):** The pair shift position, now both facing forward toward a small stone fire pit built into the cabin floor in front of them, filled with a neat stack of unlit dry firewood. The woman gently nods toward the wood, silently communicating a request to the dragon, her cold hands resting near the blanket's edge. The baby dragon tilts its head curiously at the firewood, studying it intently with an almost comically serious expression, small nostrils flaring slightly.

**Scene 3 (14–18s):** Close-up on the dragon's face — its eyes narrow slightly, nostrils twitch, and in a sudden comedic-but-magical beat, it sneezes sharply. A small burst of sparks and a quick lick of flame bursts from its nostrils/mouth, instantly catching the dry firewood alight. The fire pit ignites into a warm, crackling campfire, flickering orange light suddenly washing over both their faces, cutting through the cold blue tones of the room.

**Scene 4 (18–24s):** Both the woman and the baby dragon lean forward together toward the new fire, extending their hands/claws toward the warmth. The woman's face relaxes into a soft, relieved, affectionate smile, her cheeks now warmly lit by the flames. She glances down at the dragon with pure fondness and gratitude, pulling it slightly closer under the shared blanket. The dragon sits calmly beside her, blinking contentedly, warm firelight reflecting in its large dark eyes, steam gently rising from the heat against the cold air.

**Scene 5 (24–26s):** Final tight close-up — the dragon nestled safely in the crook of the woman's arm under the blanket, both looking toward the fire in comfortable silence, her hand resting protectively over its back. A quiet, cozy, emotionally warm moment amid the harsh snowy night outside.

**Overall tone and continuity:** A tender, slightly whimsical beat within an otherwise dark-fantasy narrative — balancing the earlier story's tension and secrecy with a moment of simple domestic comfort and humor (the dragon "sneezing" fire). Maintains consistent character design, lighting philosophy (cold blue exteriors/windows vs. warm amber interior firelight), and photorealistic creature rendering (wet-look skin, fine scale texture, anatomically grounded proportions) from the previous installments. Sound design implied: howling wind and soft snowfall outside, a small dragon sneeze/chuff sound, crackling fire, quiet breathing. 9:16 vertical aspect ratio, 24fps cinematic film grain, prestige dark-fantasy television quality.

2113579861490983262.name: Dave Martin
2113579861490983262.text:
Disclaimer: This post is a little nerdy and technical.

I build most everything now by coordinating with two AI agents.

Claude and Codex.

It still feels a little ridiculous to type that.

But that’s the job now. So here’s what it actually looks like, using a feature I shipped this week: a help center inside Crafd.

It starts with a brief.

I open Codex (Astra for design tasks) and empty my head into it. What the feature should do, where it should live, what to copy from. I’m not precious about it. Typos and all.

Here’s the actual prompt I used:

Can you please help me create a plan for support docs? Right now we have none and no help center or help link at all within the admin. I have [Linear link redacted] stubbed out for this project. My thoughts are: 
1) A (?) icon in the top right corner of the app. 
2) Which opens a docked right side bar with a search field at the top, and recent searches, then recommended links as a blank slate. 
3) Do an audit of the entire app and make a list of every reasonable help doc question. 
4) Build out content for each question. Use https://t.co/9zxVRupcxF as a template for how to bucket things, as well as a template for how each doc should be structured (numbered lists) https://t.co/Hle7w7fXo2. 
5) In addition to help docs, we should return deep links to specific functionality and settings in the help search results. 
6) There should be a toggle that allows you to switch the docked help sidebar to turn into a full-screen command prompt like UI. Once you toggle the UI, future clicks into help should show the latest UI selection. 
7) Last, we’ll also need a contact support option that shows a support form.Can you please help mock up a single page HTML mockup of this new help center feature as if it’s built out within the existing web-app admin? Please use HTML, CSS, Vanilla JS (No fancy JS or react). Please save the mockup to my desktop. For now, we can just show a few dummy help docs. We’ll build out the rest later. Any questions before you start?
Codex asks a few questions. I answer them. Then it builds a single HTML page that looks like it’s already part of the app. No framework, no build step. Just something I can click around in.

Then I react to it.

This is the part that feels most like my actual job. I click through it, notice everything that’s off, and write it all down in one message.

Some feedback: 

1) Drop: “The Crafd help center Let’s get you back to making. Find an answer. Jump to the right place.” Just start with the search bar at the top of the panel. 
2) FOr the command palette design, let’s have a blurred transparent BG with a card in the middle like this: [Image #1] But it can be wider by default. 
3) Can we animate the transition between the command palette and sidebar docked modes? 
4) Don’t use all caps for anything (like “Recent searches”). Sentence case and bold is fine. 
5) Let’s keep the keyboard shortcuts, but remove the key at the bottom. 
6) Let’s hide the search bar when we go to the contact form. and remove Contact support A little stuck? We’re here. 
7) Let’s remove the “What’s this about?” field, but add a “How did this make you feel?” field with 3-5 facial expression SVGs to choose from.

The image was a screenshot of a command palette I liked.

Here's a link to that final prototype: https://t.co/kkdoIrInCM

A couple rounds of that until I’m happy.

Then I hand it to Claude.

Claude and Codex don’t share a chat window, so they need a way to talk to each other.

They do that through a folder in the repo called /planning.

The main thing in there is a chat log. One markdown file. Claude writes an entry, then Codex writes an entry, each one stamped with the time and a verb like REVIEW or MERGE or ASK-DAVE. Nobody edits anyone else’s entry. Codex checks the file every couple of minutes. Claude watches it in the background.

Next to the log there’s a plan with checkboxes, a running list of every decision they made without me, and a list of ideas they want to come back to.

Claude is the lead. I only ever talk to Claude, and Claude relays to Codex.

Each agent works in its own copy of the repo. They open small pull requests and review each other’s work. Neither one is allowed to merge its own.

The whole system is a .gitignore'd folder of text files.

Here’s the prompt I sent Claude:

I worked with COdex to create a mockup of a new help center within web-app: /Users/davem/Desktop/Crafd Help Center.html. Here’s the prompt I used: [the same brief from above, pasted in again]
Can you please reset the chat in /planning and do the following:
1. Make a list of deep links and settings we should add and add a Linear issue under [Linear link redacted] for it.
2. Make a list of Help Docs we should create and make an issue with sub-issues for individual docs.
3. Break the HTML prototype down into individual issues that you can Codex can work on together.
4. Map out a plan for you and codex and let me know once that is all done and I’ll wake up Codex.

Claude reads the mockup, writes up the issues in Linear, maps out who does what, and posts the opening message in the chat log.

Then I wake up Codex. Codex reads the plan, agrees or pushes back, and they go.

After that, I mostly get out of the way.

They write the plan before the code, create Linear issues, open small pull requests, review each others work, and ping me when something needs a human. Whether to keep a button. What an email should say. When to push to production.

As work gets shipped, Linear issues get closed automatically.

Once complete, they do E2E testing via Chrome extensions and fix any issues that they find automatically.

For the help center, that ended up being 23 pull requests and 95 help docs. They started one afternoon. The last pull request merged this morning.

I wrote three prompts and answered a handful of questions. They built an entire fully functional feature in the style of my existing app.

I can't help but feel like this pace at which progress can be made on projects feels ridiculous compared to even 6 months ago.

Évaluation, fondée sur des grilles d’analyse et spécifique au patient, de grands modèles de langage dans le cadre du suivi longitudinal des soins en cancérologie : https://t.co/lM5xhrvVgd

"arXiv:2610.35847v1 [https://t.co/gQRNwvACTl] 26 Oct 2026
Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
Wei-Wei ZhangDepartment of Radiation Oncology, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou, ChinaPengkai WangDepartment of Computing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, ChinaYan LiDepartment of Radiation Oncology, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou, ChinaZhijie SangDepartment of Computing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, ChinaGuan-Qun ZhouDepartment of Radiation Oncology, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou, ChinaJun-Yan LiDepartment of Pathology, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou, ChinaShu-Han ZhouDepartment of Radiation Oncology, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou, ChinaPei-Wen LiuDepartment of Radiation Oncology, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou, ChinaTing-Xi TangDepartment of Radiation Oncology, Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, ChinaMin TangDepartment of Computing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, ChinaZhitian HouDepartment of Computing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, ChinaJianmin WuDepartment of Computing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, https://t.co/YfFkUkW8rk, Hong Kong, ChinaJian GuanGuanj@smu.edu.cnDepartment of Radiation Oncology, Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, ChinaLi Linlinli@sysucc.org.cnDepartment of Radiation Oncology, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou, ChinaHongxia Yanghongxia.yang@polyu.edu.hkDepartment of Computing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, https://t.co/YfFkUkW8rk, Hong Kong, ChinaYing Sunsunying@sysucc.org.cnDepartment of Radiation Oncology, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Guangzhou, ChinaAbstract
Large language models (LLMs) show promise in specialty medicine, yet existing evaluations largely focus on isolated clinical encounters rather than tracking how clinical responsibilities evolve across a longitudinal care pathway. Here we introduce NPC-RubricBench, a phase-aware benchmark for evaluating multistage clinical reasoning across the cancer care continuum, using nasopharyngeal carcinoma as a defined disease context. Curated from longitudinal records of 405 patients across two cancer centers, the benchmark comprises 941 patient-phase units across six sequential care phases and 17,688 patient-specific atomic criteria spanning five evaluation dimensions, with each assessment strictly restricted to decision-time clinical evidence. Evaluating 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs revealed that strong diagnostic performance does not carry over to downstream care. We evaluated 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs, showing that high diagnostic performance did not translate into improved downstream care. Instead, the dominant failure modes reversed across phases. Explicit decision errors dominated anatomical staging at 48.2%, whereas decision omissions dominated initial work-up and post-treatment follow-up at 33.4% and 30.4%, respectively. In the evaluated model set, medically adapted models showed higher omission rates than general-purpose models. Moreover, varying query granularity exposes a critical specification trade-off: broad open-ended requests degrade Decision Quality across all 30 models, while more detailed, checklist-like prompts raise Decision Quality but reduce Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence. Furthermore, NPC-RubricBench demonstrates that static diagnostic benchmarks are insufficient to ensure consistent clinical reliability over time, highlighting the importance of phase-adaptive safeguards in multistage medical AI.large language models, longitudinal cancer care, rubric-based evaluation, nasopharyngeal carcinomakeywords
